title: Distinct user groups
requirement: Evaluate and claim separately for (a) adults with everyday handwriting difficulty, (b) people with essential/action tremor while writing, (c) people with Parkinson's disease (micrographia, bradykinesia, tremor subtypes), (d) drawing/art users
rationale: Mechanisms and evidence differ; PD writing impairment is mainly micrographia (COR-10)
current_estimate: Groups defined in validation/human_study_plan.md

title: Active correction target population
requirement: Active nib correction claims restricted to writers whose measured writing tremor at the nib is <= 0.5 mm peak per axis (zero-to-peak, DEC-054's convention: sqrt(2) x RMS; REQ-DATA-004) for full correction, with partial correction declared up to 1 mm peak
rationale: Travel +/-0.5 mm; ~30% (15-50%) of ET patients within 1 mm p-p (PDT-12 fit); PD tremor-at-nib unknown. Restated in DEC-054's zero-to-peak convention (REQ-DATA-004); the limits are unchanged, since for a steady tremor peak-to-peak is twice zero-to-peak (human_study_plan.md s3.6: A_pp = 2 sqrt(2) A_rms). 0.5 mm peak is the lower edge of DEC-054's severe class (0.51 mm). Was: 'Active nib correction claims restricted to writers whose measured writing tremor at the nib is <= 1 mm peak-to-peak per axis (full correction) with partial correction declared up to 2 mm'
current_estimate: ET: ~30% fully (within 0.5 mm peak, 1 mm p-p), ~50% within 1 mm peak (2 mm p-p) (derived from PDT-12's peak-to-peak fit). DEC-054's classes at the tip: severe above 0.51 mm, typically 1.7 mm (REQ-DATA-004). EXP-H01 reports peak-to-peak, with DEC-054's classes beside it (EXP-R01)

title: No diagnostic function
requirement: The pen and app shall not diagnose or score disease; health-status data only with explicit research consent
rationale: Regulatory and privacy scope (report s25)

title: Writing altitude range
requirement: Assistance and capture specified for barrel altitude 35-75 deg (nominal 50 deg) at any roll and azimuth; assistance fades outside the range
rationale: Healthy adults write near 50 deg on paper and 62 +/- 7.5 deg on tablets (COR-26)
current_estimate: Design and simulation use 35-75 deg; see REQ-MECH-001 for the travel limit at low altitude

title: Normal force range
requirement: Full function for normal force 0.2-2.0 N (nominal 1.0 N); graceful saturation of assistance above the thermal and current limits
rationale: Axial writing force mean 1.0 N, writer means 0.56-2.08 N (COR-26)
current_estimate: Configuration B holds the design point but not the upper range continuously (REQ-ACT-001)

title: Tremor to be addressed by active correction
requirement: Active cancellation addresses writing tremor of 3-12 Hz and <= 1 mm peak-to-peak at the nib whose tracked frequency is above the per-user gate
rationale: Travel limit (REQ-MECH-001), addressable population (REQ-USR-002, COR-10), frequency gate (DEC-009)
current_estimate: Simulation: no causal estimator helps below ~9 Hz on synthetic writing (docs/sim_report.md s3.2)

title: Grip diameter
requirement: 14-16 mm at the grip zone (0-40 mm from tip); actuator section may reach 16 mm (Rev A bulge 16 mm at 45-57 mm)
rationale: Comfort; actuator envelope (COR-17)
current_estimate: Rev A: 15 mm grip, 16 mm bulge

title: Length
rationale: Brief
current_estimate: Rev A: 150 mm

title: Mass
requirement: <= 35 g including refill and battery, with >= 10% margin carried in the budget until weighed
rationale: Brief; mass drives comfort
current_estimate: Rev A.1 with polymer rear barrel: 33.2 g incl. allowances and 10 % contingency (37.2 g with Al barrel; Rev A 40.7 g)

title: Balance
requirement: Centre of mass within 70 mm of the tip (provisional; ordinary-pen comparison pending)
rationale: Tail-heavy pens tire the grip
current_estimate: Rev A.1 with polymer rear barrel 76.0 mm (Al barrel 79.4 mm; Rev A 80.6 mm)

title: Page correction workspace
requirement: Guaranteed page-plane correction disc of radius 0.5 mm at every altitude 35-75 deg and every roll, after calibration; reduced authority outside
rationale: Brief s2 (+/-0.5 mm per page axis); page-referenced definition (COR-03, COR-04)
verification: EXP-B04 static map with independent metrology
current_estimate: With q_lim 0.55 mm the tilt-direction page correction reachable is 0.39 / 0.45 / 0.48 / 0.50 mm at 35 / 45 / 50 / 55 deg (compliance-aware J, nominal gamma): the 0.5 mm disc holds only for theta >= 55 deg. Typical paper writing is near 50 deg (COR-26). Options: accept 0.45 mm at 45 deg, or raise q_lim toward the 0.60 mm stop (no mechanical margin).

title: Mechanical travel and stops
requirement: Hard stops at 0.60 mm tip-equivalent radius; stop loads limited so flexure stress stays below allowable at impact
rationale: Protect flexures (COR-18)
current_estimate: Rev A.1 mechanical travel 0.60 mm (tolerance analysis); control limit 0.55 mm

title: Moving mass
requirement: Tip-equivalent inertia <= 12 g
rationale: Reaction forces and bandwidth
current_estimate: 13.7 g tip-equivalent (distributed-mass CAD, Rev A.1; the earlier 10.3 g was a point-mass approximation); CFRP carrier option ~9.5 g

title: Axial load path
requirement: Axial stiffness at the nib 1-5 kN/m with force sensing; compliant range up to >= 1.4 N axial; overload stop beyond
rationale: Limit force-induced ink shift while bounding pressure modulation (COR-05). Simulated device distortion 53-59 um at 2-8 kN/m, 69-87 um at 0.3-1 kN/m (results/sim/design_sweeps.json); the earlier < 30 um target is not reachable in the current model
current_estimate: 2 kN/m, preload 0.25 N, stop at 0.6 mm (1.45 N)

title: Pressure modulation
requirement: Normal-force modulation caused by correction <= 0.15 N RMS in 3-15 Hz at the design point, subject to EXP-B08 ink-quality limit
rationale: Ink continuity and feel
current_estimate: 0.07-0.12 N RMS (simulation, literature hand)

title: Pivot flexure fatigue
requirement: Peak flexure stress <= 310 MPa at full travel and alternating <= 150 MPa at typical amplitude (0.3 mm tip), C17200 TH04
rationale: AMF allowables; 1e8 cycles
current_estimate: Gimbal candidate: 177 MPa / 82 MPa

title: Pivot buckling margin
requirement: >= 5x Euler margin for flexure elements under 2 N axial load
rationale: Axial writing load passes the pivot
current_estimate: Gimbal margin 19x

title: Refill interface
requirement: ISO 12757-2 D1 refill; kinematic seat; replacement without tools; neutral offset repeatable to <= 20 um or re-calibrated by a user routine < 30 s
rationale: Brief s6
current_estimate: Seat design pending

title: Continuous transverse load capability
requirement: React >= 0.75 N tip-equivalent transverse load continuously (design point incl. friction) and >= 1.4 N for 2 s
rationale: COR-01 loads at design and high points
current_estimate: Configuration B (Kf 0.717 N/A, n 3.17): 1.4 N needs 0.62 A per axis, above the 0.60 A software limit; 0.75 N continuous needs 0.65 W copper referenced to 20 C (0.85 W at the 96.6 C design coil) against 0.412 W allowable for a moving coil (results/thermal/thermal.json v0.4.4). Infeasible for B as a continuous rating; D (skid) and E (bias) carry the static load passively.

title: Copper loss at design point
requirement: Average actuator copper loss while writing <= 0.25 W (thermal and runtime)
rationale: Surface temperature and runtime
current_estimate: Average copper loss while writing (65 % pen-down) at the design point: B 0.33 W (0.50 W in contact); D 0.05 W; E 0.01 W (results/trade/config_trade.json, parameters v0.4.2)

title: Force bandwidth
requirement: Current loop >= 2 kHz closed-loop; position loop >= 60 Hz with reference feedforward
rationale: Tremor band 3-12 Hz with servo lag < 1 ms equivalent
current_estimate: Design: 2 kHz current, 60 Hz position

title: Local motion sensing
requirement: Housing page-plane motion measured at >= 1 kHz with <= 3 ms total latency and <= 5 um RMS noise per sample on matte paper at 35-75 deg
rationale: Estimator and delay budget
verification: EXP-S01 latency and accuracy vs tilt on paper
current_estimate: Unknown on paper; DeltaPen 24-68 um per 10 ms window on Wacom surface

title: Optical coverage vs roll
requirement: At least one optical sensor with valid view of the page at any roll angle
rationale: Pen rolls freely in hand
current_estimate: 3 sensors at 120 deg interleaved with pivot flexures

title: IMU
requirement: 6-axis IMU >= 1 kHz output, rigidly mounted to housing; used for orientation, contact events and bridging optical latency only
rationale: COR-08
current_estimate: LSM6DSV16X class

title: Stage position sensing
requirement: Lever angle measured synchronously with the 2 kHz stage loop (>= 4 kHz preferred for derivative noise, subject to the 3-axis rate of the Hall sensor, VERIFY) with <= 2 um RMS noise referred to the tip and current-crosstalk after compensation <= 5 um/A
rationale: Servo stiffness and noise; the simulator meets its stability and tracking results with 2 kHz sampling and 0.1 ms delay
current_estimate: 3-D Hall on refill rear magnet (TMAG5170 class) or 2x linear Hall

title: Axial force sensing
requirement: Axial force 0.1-2 N with <= 10 mN RMS noise at >= 500 Hz
rationale: Contact detection, feedforward, gamma estimation
verification: EXP-B05 (axial path against the F/T reference)
current_estimate: Axial slide via 3-D Hall z-channel (k_ax = 2 kN/m -> 5 um per 10 mN)

title: Position reference in the tremor band
requirement: If the tremor estimate uses a position reference (the page sensor), its error on the tremor alone at the severe class, in the tremor band (f0 +/- 2 Hz, study R's measure) and with its drift removed, is at most 0.15 mm (a hypothesis: EXP-E21 sets the number), and its accumulated drift meets REQ-RVJ-C05
rationale: DEC-069: estimator effort goes to separating tremor from writing first, then to a drift-free position reference in the tremor band; predicting the tremor over the pen's 4.9 ms horizon leaves 0.03 mm, as perfect knowledge (SIM). With the tremor alone (SIM, study F): the ideal page sensor gives 0.055 mm in band and 0.11 mm at the tip; the DeltaPen-class model 0.286 mm in band but 1.14 mm at the tip (its drift); the IMU alone 0.30 mm in band, and a perfect accelerometer does no better
verification: EXP-E21 (AC-E21-01); EXP-T04 and EXP-R07 (the die on paper)
current_estimate: No page sensor measured on paper (EXP-T04). SIM (study F, tuning split, the tremor alone): the ideal page sensor (3 um, 2 ms) 0.055 mm in band; the DeltaPen-class model 0.286 mm in band, 1.14 mm at the tip, and 0.59 mm with a causal 1.5 Hz high-pass. DEC-070: the DeltaPen-class figures used page model v1, which changed past readings and recovered lost motion from the truth; they stand only as labelled optimistic bounds, suspended as device evidence until study X reruns them with page model v2

title: Loop rates
requirement: Current regulation 40 kHz (DEC-012); stage loop 2 kHz; estimator 2 kHz; optional learned predictor 250 Hz
rationale: Brief s5
evidence_status: proposed design; host and QEMU execution
current_estimate: Firmware core runs the 40 kHz current loop and the 2 kHz stage task (60/60 test cases on host and QEMU). QEMU instruction counts: current ISR 422 mean / 446 max (at least 14 % of the 3200-cycle period at 128 MHz), stage tick 11 535 / 13 112 (at least 20 % of 64 000 cycles; 41 % of the ICD's 250 us compute budget). Instructions are not cycles; timing on the nRF5340 is unmeasured

title: Stability margins
requirement: Phase margin >= 40 deg and gain margin >= 6 dB for the loaded plant over declared contact and hand ranges
rationale: Robustness
verification: Identified plant from EXP-B05 plus a loop-margin analysis (not yet written)
current_estimate: Unloaded model: phase margin 35.3 deg, gain margin 10.9 dB (firmware closed-loop test on the simulator gains, results/firmware/test_report.txt) -> phase margin below 40 deg; loaded plant pending EXP-B05

title: Effective delay
requirement: Effective delay from housing motion to nib correction <= 5 ms in 3-12 Hz including servo lag
rationale: Brief s2
current_estimate: Prediction horizon 1.33 ms (IMU 1 ms + half stage period + current loop); delay-limited residual at 8 Hz 0.07 -> delay not the limit

title: Authority limiting
requirement: Correction bounded by travel taper, slew limit, confidence, contact state and thermal governor; no model output bypasses limits
rationale: Brief s11 s12
evidence_status: proposed design; host and QEMU execution
current_estimate: Limiter tested on host and QEMU: |q| <= q_lim + 0.5 nm over 4000 radii; slew <= 40 um per tick over 2000 random slews. ML outputs pass the same limits (guard rules 2-3); the thermal governor derates authority

title: Intent preservation
requirement: Intended-path distortion caused by assistance (no disturbance present) <= 50 um RMS and corner/dot position error <= 100 um on the feature course; deliberate fast features (hatching, fast strokes) <= 150 um max (provisional until EXP-H05 perception thresholds)
rationale: Preserve deliberate features
verification: simulation feature course; EXP-B09; EXP-E02; EXP-H05
current_estimate: Simulation (Rev A, parameters v0.4.4, 12 test seeds): Kalman 100 um RMS distortion on tremor-free writing (55 um on the 4 nominal seeds; both tuning profiles now select the same set), band-pass 168 um -> violates 50 um. Learned TCN 14.5 um RMS but spikes of 125 um at corners on the feature course (above the 100 um limit; ML results v0.4.1)

title: Compliance-aware Jacobian
requirement: Page-to-stage mapping uses identified gamma (suspension/hand compliance ratio) and measured tilt; identification converges within 2 s of writing
rationale: COR-04
current_estimate: Fixed gamma from nominal compliances in simulation

title: Frequency-gated authority
requirement: Tremor cancellation authority gated by tracked tremor frequency relative to a per-user threshold from calibration
rationale: COR-11
current_estimate: Gate tuned on tuning seeds

title: Guided mode capture distance
requirement: Guided (known-path) assistance only within a capture radius of the registered path with user-paced progress; releases authority outside
rationale: Brief s11 s16; HAP-18
current_estimate: Simulator mode 6: circle path distance 443 -> 163 um (results/sim/guided_path_distance.json). Firmware guided.c: template-tracking test passes on host and QEMU. Bench AC-B09-11/12 pending

title: Causal commands
requirement: Every nose command at a control tick uses only sensor samples available at that tick (acquisition time + latency <= tick time); estimator outputs are computed at the tick or extrapolated causally
rationale: A look-ahead of even 1-2 ms flatters estimators in simulation; study L found and fixed two such leaks before its test
verification: Unit tests that change future samples (ai2/tests); firmware replay test (EXP-L01)
current_estimate: Met in the study's code after two fixes (detector window, delayed-ink interpolation); ai2/tests checks the causality of the smoother, detector, learned models, output extrapolation and policies; firmware not yet written

title: Tremor-line gate stays shut on writing
requirement: The tremor-line gate stays closed for >= 99 % of tremor-free writing time for every writer; with it the pen moves tremor-free writing no more than the Rev H tracker + 2 um RMS
rationale: The listening estimator reads some writing rhythms as tremor (259 um on tremor-free writing without the gate, SIM); the gate must keep the Rev H tracker's behaviour there
verification: EXP-L01; SIM stages cl and test
current_estimate: Never open on the tremor-free writing of any tuning or test writer; tremor-free writing moved 26.3 um, as with the Rev H tracker (SIM, synthetic glyph writers). This Rev H baseline is above the 15 um of REQ-RVH-006 and the 25 um of REQ-ML-001 (other writer models). Real writing (study R, HW1 with real inputs, UNIPEN test writers): Rev H and Rev J gated moved it 25 um (14-42), the gate shut 99.8 % of the time (SIM, docs/real_data.md)

title: Gated tracker worth the risk
requirement: At 1-2 mm tremor (6-10 Hz) the ink error is <= 0.8 x the Rev H tracker's, letters read >= Rev H's - 1 point at every condition, and 0.3 mm tremor no worse than 1.02 x Rev H's
rationale: The gain must be worth the risk (study L rules R2 and R3)
current_estimate: 430 against 627 um at 1-2 mm (0.69; paired -197 um, 95 % CI -206 to -188); 6 Hz 818 -> 540 um; letters read 64 -> 78 %, words 49 -> 74 %; 0.3 mm 161 against 162 um (SIM, test writers 0-5, seeds 200-203). Real inputs (study R, SIM): at the severe class (1.72 mm) the gated tracker left 0.96 x and the Rev H tracker 1.06 x of the ordinary pen's tip tremor, with 0.4 of 10 words read for both; at 1 mm 1.03-1.04 x against 1.08 x (docs/real_data.md)

title: Ink lag limits (only if delayed ink is revived)
requirement: Applies only if delayed ink is ever revived (DEC-042: the ink never trails the hand): the ink lag is <= 25 ms while writing, returns to 0 within 5 ms of the hand stopping or lifting, and keeps the hand-ink distance within the usable nose travel for >= 99 % of pen-down time
rationale: Perception: people notice inking lag from a median of about 50 ms (HAP-90); a 100 ms lag cut stroke ends (54 % of words) and beyond 25 ms the hand-ink distance exceeds +/-3 mm (SIM, CALC)
current_estimate: Not adopted. <= 25 ms: -4 % ink error (430 -> 412 um) and no more words (73 against 74 %), failed the letters rule on confirmation seed 301; the command exceeded 3 mm for 3.5 % of pen-down time at 25 ms and 6 mm for at most 0.65 % at any lag (SIM)

title: Guidance fades and hands back
requirement: Guidance level fades across sessions with the writer's own error (forgetting factor f < 1 and a tolerance band), and guidance drops to 0 within 60 ms of the writer staying > 2.5 mm from the target
rationale: Assistance as needed and hand-back (HAP-94, EML-59); a per-letter assistance-as-needed law reacted one letter late (SIM)
current_estimate: Partial guidance (0.5) brought the ink 29 % closer to the target letters (582 -> 413 um) with no loss of letters read (92.9 %); per-letter assistance as needed gave the same share of help (24.9 %) and less gain on malformed letters (0.47 against 0.54) (SIM, passive hand: fading across sessions not testable)

title: The pen writes an accepted word whole
requirement: Whole words are written by a grounded stage or a moving page (DEC-071: the grounded five-bar, EXP-BB07; the platen, EXP-PL05); in-pen autowrite of whole words stays a bench research mode with the C1S nose (DEC-050) and makes no executable claim. Any mechanism writes an accepted word only after the writer has explicitly accepted that revision (DEC-074: a proposal changes nothing until accepted; stale or tampered proposals fail; ink already on the paper is never erased), and only if (a) the tallest letter fits the usable reach (the stage's reach minus a 0.5 mm reserve), (b) each letter is admitted whole before it starts, and (c) it slows or waits when the hand lags, lifts after 0.5 s without progress, and hands back after 2 s without progress or when the hand runs ahead; it never leaves half a letter; a supervisor stops it on stale sensing, lost anchoring, tracking, current or temperature limits (DEC-074)
rationale: Rule C1 of study S; the review's s10. Reach decides: at a 3 mm x-height a whole accepted word needs about +/-4-6 mm of nib reach with the hand advancing as usual (95 % written in full at +/-6 mm, 23 % at +/-4 mm, 0 % at +/-1-2 mm; 2 % with a still hand), so the travel comes from the hand's sweep (DEC-049, DEC-056 (f)); REQ-RVJ-N01's guaranteed 6.0 mm is the reach that works. This is the plan of REQ-RVJ-N07's autowrite; its hand-backs count in its coverage and completion time (REQ-WP-011). DEC-050 (2026-09-30) makes autowrite a bench research mode with the C1S nose until a low-power large-reach design exists; the text after the prefix is unchanged. DEC-071 (the lead, 2026-09-30): in-pen autowrite of whole accepted words is superseded as an executable claim; all historic +/-6 mm completions violated the sampled motion limits (95th-percentile peak acceleration 36.7 m/s^2 against 2 m/s^2), and the new planner admits 5 of 520 glyphs at 1.5 mm and 0 at 1.059 mm. DEC-074: corrections are proposed, then explicitly accepted. Was (DEC-050): 'Bench research mode with the C1S nose (DEC-050: autowrite needs about +/-4-6 mm of reach, which the product's B1 nib does not have): The pen writes an accepted word only if (a) the tallest letter fits the usable reach (the stage's reach minus a 0.5 mm reserve), (b) each letter is admitted whole before it starts, and (c) it slows or waits when the hand lags, lifts after 0.5 s without progress, and hands back after 2 s without progress or when the hand runs ahead; it never leaves half a letter'
source: DEC-056 (f); DEC-049; DEC-050; docs/spelling_and_clarity.md (T9; rule C1; proposed requirements); DEC-071; DEC-074; docs/writing_improvement_audit.md
verification: ai3/complete_plan.py; ai3/accepted_completion.py; EXP-BB07 (the grounded five-bar); EXP-PL05 (the platen, AC-PL05-04: acceptance and the supervisor); EXP-S19 (AC-S19-01, AC-S19-02) only as bench research with the C1S module
current_estimate: Kinematics only (SIM): 100 completions in 20 test writers' own letters at a 3 mm x-height (median 11.8 mm for the pen to write); with letter admission 0 half letters per 100 completions with steady, slow or still hands and 8 with hands that pause or run ahead, against 2-99 point by point (at +/-6 mm); the pen takes 1.01 x the writer's own time with a steady hand. No stage dynamics or tremor. DEC-070: none of these is device evidence (causal sensing is the default, and results computed with ideal sensing are not device evidence). The grounded five-bar wrote 20 of 20 accepted 'se' suffixes with no resisting hand and 0 of 20 against a 200 or 500 N/m grip (SIM, the independent pass: rigid links, ideal current loops); the platen 20 of 20 with the pen docked in a cradle (SIM, study P)
trace: DEC-056; ai3/complete_plan.py; ai3/tests/test_words_plan.py; results/ai3/ai3.json; DEC-071; DEC-074; ai3/accepted_completion.py; ai3/completion_replay.py

title: Estimator accepted on its worst held-out writer
requirement: A tremor estimator is accepted only if its worst held-out writer meets the clean-writing limit (DEC-055: <= 50 um), not only the mean; its tuning set spans the letter sizes and speeds of the population it will meet (at least the 5-95 % range of the held-out writers)
rationale: The frozen design met 18 um mean and 40 um worst on 5 tuning writers but moved one test writer's clean writing 493 um: that writer's letters were 2 x larger and 1.5 x faster than any tuning writer's (SIM, docs/real_tracker.md s7, s15)
source: DEC-055; DEC-060; DEC-061; docs/real_tracker.md (s18, proposed requirements)
verification: per-writer table of the results card; writer statistics of the tuning and test sets (EXP-E10, AC-E10-01)
current_estimate: Study E (SIM, HW1 with real inputs): the frozen design (ai2's TCN with a soft size gate) moved clean writing 18.0 um on average (40.5 um on the worst note) on the 5 tuning writers, and 68.2 um on average with 493 um for one of the 9 test writers, whose 15 mm letters were about 2 x larger and 1.5 x faster than the tuning writers' (3.4-7.4 mm, slow)

title: Authority gate calibrated on the user's own writing
requirement: The nose's authority gate is calibrated on the user's own clean writing (a short tremor-free or low-tremor sample, or the first minutes of use in shadow mode) before it may act: the gate's opening threshold sits above the estimator's output on that writing
rationale: Size thresholds fixed on a few writers do not transfer (docs/real_tracker.md s7, s15); ai2's TCN without a gate moved the 9 test writers' clean writing by 40-583 um (SIM). Study E modelled the Rev J nose; the rule applies to whatever nib the estimator drives, B1 in Rev K (DEC-050)
verification: shadow-mode log of the estimate's size on clean writing; EXP-E11 (AC-E11-01, AC-E11-02); REQ-CTRL-019 (raise-only, DEC-068; AC-E11-03)
current_estimate: Study F (SIM, information only: study E had seen the test writers; EXP-E11): with per-user raise-only calibration the largest clean-writing change over 9 test writers was 19.1 um (ai2's TCN) and 18.9 um (the real-data TCN), and a rule that could lower the threshold moved one writer 60.5 um (DEC-068, REQ-CTRL-019). Before study F: the frozen design's gate, set on the 5 tuning writers, was on average half open (mean authority 0.50) on one test writer's clean note and moved it 0.49 mm (SIM, docs/real_tracker.md s7)

title: No tracker adds tremor beyond the nose held
requirement: Every tracker result reports the nose-held pen beside the ordinary pen, and a tracker may not raise the tip tremor above the nose-held pen at the mild and moderate classes for any held-out writer (<= 1.02 x)
rationale: The heavier pen alone adds 8-9 %; the frozen design added up to 4.6 x at the mild class for one writer (SIM, docs/real_tracker.md s3, s9). In Rev K the reference is the same pen with the B1 nib held (DEC-050)
verification: results card rows 'nose held' and per-writer ratios (EXP-R02, AC-R02-07, which also scores EXP-E10's run)
current_estimate: Study E, test split (SIM): the Rev J pen with the nose held 1.08 x the ordinary pen's tip tremor at every class; G4 1.07-1.08 x; the frozen design 1.13 x (moderate) and 1.32 x (mild) on average, up to 4.6 x the nose-held pen at the mild class for one writer and 1.13 x for another

title: Tremor left at the tip by a severe-tremor tracker
requirement: A tracker offered for severe tremor leaves at most 0.55 mm of tremor at the tip (study R's measure: sqrt(2) x RMS along the major axis of ink minus intended, in contact, f0 +/- 2 Hz) at the severe class on held-out real inputs, PD and ET pooled and each reported, with DEC-055's clean-writing lines; 0.25 mm for near-normal reading
rationale: DEC-067: study F's level for DEC-055's +2 words at the severe class, about a third of the class's 1.72 mm (SIM, HW1 with real inputs, the literal AI reader standing in for people). The tuning split put it at 0.65 mm (0.56-0.70), confirmed once on the test split (a gain of 1.98 words at 0.65 mm), whose own curve gives 0.55 mm (0.47-0.64; PD 0.46, ET 0.62); 80 % of the tremor-free words were read at 0.25-0.26 mm. DEC-055 stays the pass line, because a correction that moves the writing can meet a tip-tremor number and still lose every word: a linear filter left 0.72 mm but moved clean writing 2.4 mm, and no word was read (SIM)
verification: EXP-E10's results card (AC-E10-03); EXP-E20 (AC-E20-01, people reading the E13 inks)
current_estimate: SIM (study F, test split): the ordinary pen leaves 1.64 mm at the severe class, study E's best causal tracker 1.12 mm and perfect knowledge 0.03 mm. With Rev K's +/-1.0 mm nib even perfect knowledge leaves 1.00 mm (study F s8: the Rev J nose with its travel cut, tuning split)

title: Gate calibration only raises the threshold
requirement: Per-user calibration of the authority gate only ever raises the design's opening threshold; the rule (quantile and margin) is fixed per design on tuning writers
rationale: DEC-068 (refines DEC-061 and REQ-CTRL-016). In study F's simulation (information only: study E had seen the test writers) the raise-only rules kept every test writer's clean writing within 19.1 um (ai2's TCN; 493.0 um with its frozen gate) and 18.9 um (the real-data TCN), while a rule that could also lower the threshold moved one writer 60.5 um, above DEC-055's 50 um cap. A user who cannot write without tremor has no clean writing to calibrate on (EXP-E22)
verification: firmware review (AC-E11-03); EXP-E11 in simulation and on the EXP-R01 shadow-mode logs (AC-E11-02); EXP-E22 (AC-E22-01)
current_estimate: SIM, information only (study F, 9 test writers): with raise-only rules the largest clean-writing change was 19.1 um (ai2's TCN) and 18.9 um (the real-data TCN), and the worst writer's mild-tremor ratio to the held nib 1.004 (2.892 with the frozen gate); no words were gained at the severe class (-0.22 and +0.11); the listening AKF's per-user rule lowered the threshold for 4 of 9 writers and moved one writer 60.5 um

title: Learned model gate
requirement: A learned predictor may be enabled only if, on held-out participants (EXP-H01 recordings, EXP-E01 protocol), it reduces the residual ratio by >= 0.10 with the 95 % paired-bootstrap upper bound below 0, in each of the 4-8 Hz and 8-12 Hz bands, at matched false correction (<= 25 um RMS on tremor-free writing) against the best conventional estimator (Kalman, BMFLC, scheduled least-squares), and without false-correction spikes above 100 um. Gate fixed before any real data is analysed.
rationale: Brief s12 s17
current_estimate: Synthetic data: TCN meets the gate in distribution (all-band 0.48 vs 0.76, paired difference -0.28 [-0.33, -0.24]) but fails under shift (0.83 vs 0.87, n.s.) and in the coupled simulator (3-15 Hz: 0.73 vs 0.77); corner spikes 125 um. Not met: no real data. Real inputs (study R, SIM): the TCN trained on synthetic writers moved clean real writing 172 um (93-286) and left 0.71 x of the ordinary pen's tip tremor at the severe class (docs/real_data.md)

title: Inference budget
requirement: Learned predictor <= 1 ms worst-case at 128 MHz per 4 ms step, <= 64 kB RAM, streaming state, output with timestamp/expiry/confidence
rationale: EML findings
verification: On-target benchmark on the nRF5340 (not yet run); QEMU instruction count only so far (results/ml/budget.json)
current_estimate: Exported TCN (tcn_s_nofest, inputs dx/dy only): 16.2 k MAC, 7.3 kB weights, 0.58 kB RAM; 0.27-0.86 ms with CMSIS-NN (estimated), 0.90-1.44 ms plain C (115 k QEMU instructions per inference; not cycle-accurate); C bit-exact vs Python int8 on 20 000 windows
trace: results/ml/budget.json; results/ml/export_c.json; docs/icd.md s5 (output carries timestamp, expiry and confidence)

title: Learned estimator on the pen
requirement: A learned tremor estimator is causal, takes <= 2 ms per 2 ms step on the pen MCU (int8) with <= 64 kB of weights, and may drive the nose only after REQ-ML-001 passes on held-out real recordings; until then it runs in shadow mode (computed and logged, not driving the nose)
rationale: Compute and safety; the TCN was trained and tested inside one simulator family
current_estimate: TCN: 34 k parameters, 33 248 MAC per 2 ms step, 33 kB of int8 weights + about 16 kB of history, about 0.56 ms per step on a 128 MHz Cortex-M33 (28 % of one core; CALC, ASSUMPTION MCU model); REQ-ML-002 allows <= 1 ms per 4 ms step. SIM: 278 um at 1-2 mm; tremor-free writing moved 19.3 um on average but 34.8 um for the worst writer (above REQ-ML-001's 25 um)

title: RL arbitration gate
requirement: No learned policy drives the nib; the model-based causal controller stays (DEC-073, refining DEC-042). Learning may return only as a bounded residual on the causal controller that, after the plant is identified on the bench, beats the frozen rules on untouched writers and seeds in closed loop: it meets REQ-CTRL-010 and REQ-CTRL-011 and beats the controller by >= 5 %
rationale: Replay rewards did not predict closed-loop false correction (SIM). DEC-073 (the lead, 2026-09-30): six PPO policies across two frozen protocols (245,760 training transitions) failed their adoption rules, and the earlier reward, which stopped charging tracking error when contact was lost, is corrected. Was (DEC-042): 'No RL policy drives the nose (DEC-042). An RL policy may arbitrate assistance on the pen only if, in closed loop on held-out writers and seeds, it meets REQ-CTRL-010 and REQ-CTRL-011 and beats the model-based gate by >= 5 %'
current_estimate: Replay-trained PPO arbiter: 298 um and 89 % of words at 1-2 mm, but tremor-free writing moved 30.7 um (60.9 um on tuning) and worse than Rev H at 10 Hz, 0.3 mm: fails rules R1 and R2; residual RL moved tremor-free writing by 165 um (SIM). No closed-loop training yet. The independent pass (SIM, synthetic writers): six PPO policies failed their adoption rules (DEC-073)

title: Runtime
requirement: >= 60 min active writing at the design point with the qualified cell
rationale: Brief s2
verification: power budget; EXP-P01 (measured power and duty cycle)
current_estimate: B: 81 min writing at 65 % pen-down duty (54 min continuous contact) at the design point; D: 215 min; E: 277 min (200 mAh x 0.8 usable, 115 mW electronics; results/trade/config_trade.json v0.4.2)

title: Cell current capability
requirement: Cell rated for >= 2 A pulse and >= 1 A continuous with protection IC
rationale: Actuator peaks (COR-14)
verification: EXP-P02 (cell qualification, charging and battery safety pre-compliance)
current_estimate: Peak cell current ~0.8 A (2 coils + electronics) -> pouch rated >= 5 C; 10440 cells limited to ~1 C (COR-14)

title: Actuation during charging
requirement: Actuation disabled while charging in research builds
rationale: Brief s10
evidence_status: proposed design; host and QEMU execution
current_estimate: Hardware: ACT_EN = REQ.FAULT_N.NOCHG removes VMOT while charging (schematic). Firmware: system test (e) passes on host and QEMU; actuation is off while charging and re-arming is refused until unplug

title: Touch temperature
requirement: Continuously held surfaces <= 43 C absolute in a rated maximum room of 30 C, that is <= 13 K above the room (ECMA-287 B.5), with 41 C (11 K) as the design target; on the Rev J pen checked at the web over the coil plate
rationale: ECMA-287 Table 5.2: continuously held parts, all materials, 43 C (from EN 563; continuous holding below 8 h); its B.5 lets the maker rate a room above 25 C, and the check becomes T - T_room <= 43 - T_rated; IEC 60601-1: 41 C needs no justification. One rule for every held surface (DEC-045). Was: <= 41 C design target, 43 C absolute at 25 C ambient (provisional; regulatory review)
verification: thermal model; EXP-B07; EXP-D06; EXP-J13 (the web, Rev J.1)
current_estimate: See results/thermal. Rev J.1 (DEC-045): the web over the coil plate 35.9 C at 1 mm tremor in a 30 C room with the 0.1 mm graphite sheet in the shell wall; autowrite with 2 mm tremor 43.7 C (CALC, fin model); suspended by DEC-046 (the static side load of REQ-RVJ-N10 is not in it). DEC-050 (study B): B1 at 35 deg in a 30 C room, skin 30.6 C after 30 min (CALC) and 30.8 C with 2 mm tremor (SIM + CALC); REQ-BNIB-010 states B1's line

title: Coil temperature
requirement: Coil hot-spot <= 120 C (class B margin) including moving-coil air-gap resistance
rationale: Magnet demagnetisation and insulation
current_estimate: Moving coil 96.6 C at the design load, 65 % pen-down (thermal network v0.4.4, 0.50 mm air gaps); the 120 C limit sets the 0.412 W allowable; overload (2 N, 35 deg) reaches 120 C in about 17 s without derating (one-node extrapolation of F5)

title: Independent actuator disable
requirement: Hardware disable of both bridges independent of firmware on over-current, over-temperature or watchdog
rationale: Brief s9
current_estimate: Hardware AND gate ACT_EN = REQ.FAULT_N.NOCHG on the load switch (schematic sheet fault_handling); ngspice: trip 8.8 us, VMOT off 22.6 us after a coil short. Firmware host test of the latch model: it clears only with ACT_EN_REQ low and is declared FAILED after 3 retries

title: Current limits
requirement: Software limit 0.60 A per axis; independent hardware trip at +/-0.80 A
rationale: Thermal and cell
current_estimate: Software limit 0.60 A per axis; independent window-comparator latch at +/-0.80 A

title: Stale or invalid model output
requirement: Expired, NaN, saturated or low-confidence model outputs reduce authority smoothly within 20 ms and never exceed deterministic limits
rationale: Brief s15
verification: unit tests with injected faults; EXP-F02
evidence_status: proposed design; host and QEMU execution
current_estimate:
Guard v1.2 in firmware:
- NaN/Inf and int16 output saturation are rejected at the next 2 kHz tick, and outputs expire at t_acq + 8 ms.
- On running-RMS inconsistency the guard falls back to the Kalman estimate 38.5 ms after a bad predictor starts; the Kalman is fully in use 20 ms later, and the predictor is re-admitted after at least 1 s.
- Confidence rule (5) normalises to byte/255 and slews over 20 ms.
Tested on host and QEMU with injected good, bad, NaN, saturated, stale and low-confidence predictors

title: Power-loss behaviour
requirement: On brown-out or fault during contact, ramp actuator current down over >= 30 ms using hold-up energy; document the resulting mark length; controlled shutdown preferred at lift
rationale: COR-19
current_estimate: Simulated power loss in contact moves the ink up to ~0.8 mm within 50 ms (F3). The firmware state machine implements the rule: low-battery and thermal faults hold neutral in contact and de-energise only after pen-up or a 5 s timeout. System fault sequences (b) and (c) pass on host and QEMU

title: Original stroke record
requirement: Immutable timestamped record of estimated nib page position incl. measured nib offset, uncertainty, contact, force, calibration and firmware/model versions
rationale: Brief s5 s16
current_estimate: ICD v1 stroke sample lacks nib-offset and uncertainty fields (planned for v2, docs/icd.md s4.6); format error RMS 3.6 um, max 120.6 um (81.5 um with pen-down/up samples; results/app/capture_fidelity.json)

title: Offline buffering and recovery
requirement: Local capture continues without phone; append-only blocks with CRC; power loss loses <= 1 block; sync idempotent; storage-full never silently deletes unsynced pages
rationale: Brief s2 s16
current_estimate: Record framing with CRC-16 and resynchronisation is implemented and tested (firmware log_format.c; the app reader resyncs after corruption; golden log round-trips byte-identically). Not implemented: flash block storage, power-loss behaviour, sync and the storage-full policy, because no flash or BLE driver exists yet

title: Page identity
requirement: Research builds use coded paper or external reference for absolute pose; ordinary-paper relocalisation treated as research risk
rationale: COR-16; OPT findings
current_estimate: Ncode/Anoto licensing costs noted

title: Recognition

rationale: Brief s16
current_estimate: ML Kit default candidate

rationale: Brief s16

title: Useful text suggestions
requirement: Next-word or word-completion suggestions reach >= 30 % top-3 accuracy on the user's own notes before they are shown by default, at <= 20 ms per suggestion on the phone
rationale: Weak suggestions cost more than they save (EML-63); here 18-28 % top-3 before the first letter (CALC)
verification: EXP-L06; EXP-S14 (the personalised model over 4 weeks); CALC
current_estimate: Next word before its first letter: 9-15 % top-1 and 18-28 % top-3 for every model (below 30 %); word completion after the first letters not yet measured. Per query on the study's CPU (one shared thread): next word 1.1 ms (larger-corpus n-gram) and 115 ms (mixture), letter two ahead 34 and 74 ms (CALC); phone not measured. Study S (CALC on two public-domain journals standing in for notes): word completion after one letter 52-56 % top-3 with the personalised model and 46-47 % with NG0, 2.2-3.0 ms at the 95th percentile on the study's CPU; the next word before its first letter 22-24 %: completions meet the line, next words do not (docs/spelling_and_clarity.md T4)

title: Synthetic handwriting labelled and legible
requirement: Synthesised handwriting is always labelled as synthetic, and is legible to the app's recogniser for >= 95 % of letters
rationale: Honesty; usefulness (96 % here, CALC); immutable originals and provenance (DEC-017)
current_estimate: Sigma-lognormal synthesis from 1 or 3 of the writer's own letters: 96 % legible to the app's recogniser; writer identified among six in 92-96 % of cases on synthetic, font-based writers, which flatters identification (CALC); the spread-tuning rule Y1 failed (the perturbation costs legibility on some letters)

title: Ink record, transcript and writing plan kept apart
requirement: The ink record, the transcript and the pen's writing plan are separate stores: the ink record is append-only and verifiable; every transcript change is logged and can be undone; a writing plan exists only for text the writer accepted
rationale: The independent review (s10), adopted by study S (DEC-056 (a), (f)). Permanent ink cannot be corrected by moving the nib, so the record of what the pen did on each stroke (nothing, nudged, withheld ink, wrote an accepted word) must never change afterwards, and what the app reads must stay apart from what the writer decides the text should say. It extends REQ-PNC-008 (autocorrect only in a derived layer) and DEC-017 (immutable originals and provenance) to the pen's writing plan
source: DEC-056; docs/spelling_and_clarity.md (the three outputs; proposed requirements); independent review 2026-09-29 s10
verification: ai3/tests/test_layers.py; the demo's smoke test; code review of the firmware and app; EXP-S18 (AC-S18-04)
current_estimate: ai3/layers.py specifies the three stores (StrokeRecord, Transcript, WritingPlan); its tests check the append-only, hash-chained record and tamper detection, the audited and undoable transcript, protected words never flagged, the auto mode only when opted in and confident, plans only from a writer's acceptance, and plans that a new prediction cannot change; the prototype page passes 28 of 28 smoke-test checks (test). Not yet in the pen's firmware or the app

title: Recognition reported before spelling cues
requirement: Recognition is reported as CER and WER on held-out people and held-out sessions, with and without the language model, before any spelling cue is on by default
rationale: Recognition is the weak link of spelling help: when the pen reads the letters itself, recognition errors look like misspellings (with raw recognised letters, mid-word cues fired about 40 times per 100 correct words, SIM). The review's gate G7. It extends REQ-APP-001 (the recogniser evaluated on target users before adoption; EXP-C01 tests the app's default recogniser) to the pen's own streaming recogniser, with sessions held out as well as people (REQ-DATA-001). DEC-056 is revisited if more than 20 % of words are read wrong (EXP-S17)
source: DEC-056; docs/spelling_and_clarity.md (T7; proposed requirements); independent review 2026-09-29 (G7)
verification: EXP-S17 (AC-S17-01; the accuracy lines AC-S17-02, AC-S17-03)
current_estimate: SIM on real letters of 20 held-out UJI writers, words assembled with ASSUMED print spacing: CER 9.1 % and WER 19.8 % with the language model, 22.9 % and 54.7 % without (writer-disjoint); calibrated on the writer's other session 9.2 % and 20.2 % (session-disjoint); tight spacing 10.5 % and 22.5 %. Joined-up writing and the pen's own recordings not yet tested (EXP-S17)

title: Spelling help: few false alarms, calibrated, abstains
requirement: Spelling help: <= 2 false alarms per 100 correct words; names, numbers and words the writer marks are never flagged; P(misspelled) is calibrated, with ECE <= 0.05 on held-out users; below the threshold it abstains; in the opt-in automatic mode <= 0.5 correct words are changed per 100
rationale: DEC-056 (c): the pen should ask, not act, at today's reading accuracy (study S, T8). Names were the commonest false alarm (12 of 43 on 4 tuning children, rule S2). Relation: REQ-PNC-008 and EXP-A03 (autocorrect of recognition errors in a derived layer, posterior >= 0.9 by default; AC-A03-02 allows 0.1 % of correctly recognised words changed, upper bound 0.5 %) cover the app's autocorrect; this requirement covers spelling help, whose opt-in automatic mode is judged per 100 correct words. DEC-074 (the lead, 2026-09-30): corrections are proposed, then explicitly accepted, so the opt-in automatic mode is not offered unless DEC-074 is revisited (EXP-S sessions show acceptance too slow); its 0.5 per 100 line (AC-S18-03) is judged only then
source: DEC-056; docs/spelling_and_clarity.md (T2, T8; rules S2, W2-W5; proposed requirements)
verification: EXP-S12 (AC-S12-02); EXP-S20 (AC-S20-01); EXP-S18 (the automatic mode, AC-S18-03)
current_estimate: Letters known exactly: 63 % of 11 test children's real misspellings caught at 2.3 false alarms per 100 correct words (CALC; the rule aimed at 2 and got 1.7 on the tuning children). The pen's own reading: 34 % caught at 1.7 per 100 (new writer) and 28 % at 2.3 (calibrated); ECE 0.06-0.08 raw and 0.03 after Platt scaling; the opt-in automatic mode changed no correct word and fixed almost nothing (SIM; post-hoc rule W5, to confirm in EXP-S20)

title: Suggestions only at natural pauses
requirement: Suggestions and completions are offered only at natural pauses (no pop-up while a letter is being written), at most 3 at a time, accepted with one accessible action (tap, key or pen gesture), and optionally read aloud
rationale: DEC-056 (d), (e); the review's R20 (accuracy against fluency). A tick at the next pause with up to 3 suggestions fixed 3.0 of 10 misspellings on paper with no cue while a word was being written, against 3.4 for a tick plus a pen lift with 7.7 cues felt mid-word per 100 words (SIM, writer responses ASSUMED); EXP-S18 compares them with writers. Weak suggestions cost more than they save (LIT EML-63; REQ-APP-003)
source: DEC-056; docs/spelling_and_clarity.md (T3, T4; rules S4, P2, I1; proposed requirements)
verification: EXP-S18 (AC-S18-05; the comparison AC-S18-01); app design review
current_estimate: Tick at the next pause with up to 3 suggestions: 3.0 of 10 misspellings fixed on paper (1.6-4.0 over the assumed responses), 6.4 suggestion lists read per 100 words, +17 % writing time (SIM, 11 test children's real errors). The prototype page offers completions at pauses (28 of 28 smoke-test checks)

title: Splits
requirement: Splits by participant and session before windowing; held-out devices/refills/papers for generalisation tests; seeds recorded
rationale: Brief s13
current_estimate: Implemented for synthetic writers in ml/datasets.py; participant/session splits apply to EXP-H01 data

title: Real inputs for every writing claim
requirement: Every tracker or pen claim about writing is also evaluated on real recorded writing and real recorded tremor (the realdata library or better), on test writers and test subjects only, and reported next to the synthetic result as a results card: words read by a literal reader out of 10, tremor left at the tip in mm, and how much clean writing changed (DEC-054)
rationale: The synthetic writers and tremor model differ from real ones in ways that change the results: at 1 mm the Rev J gated tracker left 0.68 x the ordinary pen's tip tremor with synthetic writing and tremor, 0.72 x with real writing, 1.03 x with real tremor as well and 1.04 x with the DeltaPen-class page sensor; the TCN 0.36 -> 0.54 -> 0.82 -> 0.83 x (SIM, docs/real_data.md, the bridge). Results on synthetic writers or tremor are labelled as model-input results (DEC-054). At the severe class a legibility claim needs DEC-055's pass line (AC-R02-01). DEC-070: the DeltaPen-class figures used page model v1, which changed past readings and recovered lost motion from the truth; they stand only as labelled optimistic bounds, suspended as device evidence until study X reruns them with page model v2
source: DEC-054; DEC-055; docs/real_data.md (proposed requirements; the bridge)
verification: results card with both input sets (EXP-R02: AC-R02-01, AC-R02-02)
current_estimate: Severe class (1.72 mm at the tip), real inputs, readable words out of 10: ordinary pen 0.5, Rev H 0.4, Rev J gated 0.4, TCN 0.2; perfect knowledge 7.0; the same notes without tremor 6.8 (SIM, 9 test writers, PD and ET pooled). The earlier headline on synthetic inputs: Rev J gated cut the ink error at 1-2 mm from 830 to 430 um, and 74 % of words were read instead of 31 % (SIM, results/ai2/ai2.json)

title: Clean writing for false correction
requirement: False correction ('clean writing changed') on real writing is measured on real tremor-free writing recorded on paper with a clean digitiser: <= 2.5 % of its pen-down velocity energy at 8-12 Hz, checked with sim2j.writers.kinematics before use
rationale: BRUSH's timing artefact (35.6 % of its pen-down velocity energy at 8-12 Hz) made the trackers move clean ink by 160-880 um; real writing on paper carries 1.3-1.7 % (LIT CON-25). This requirement sets the writing on which false correction is measured, not its limit. The limits stay: on real writing the absolute 25 um of the false-correction convention (validation/README.md s2; AC-E01-09, REQ-ML-001, and DEC-055's line); in sim2 REQ-RVJ-C02 (25 um against the device-off pen); REQ-CTRL-010's relative bound (Rev H + 2 um) only for HW1 on synthetic writers. Study R's selection rule also asks <= 3 % above 12 Hz, 15-60 mm/s and writing on paper
source: DEC-054; DEC-055; docs/real_data.md (the writing library); LIT CON-25
verification: kinematics check before use (realdata.kinematics; EXP-R02, AC-R02-03)
current_estimate: UNIPEN hpb2 (ballpoint on paper, 100 samples/s) 2.4 % and UCI Character Trajectories 1.3 % pass; BRUSH 35.6 % and the synthetic writers 10.1-17.3 % fail (CALC on DATA)

title: Tremor class in mm at the tip
requirement: Claims name the tremor class in mm at the pen tip (peak = sqrt(2) x RMS of the major axis in f0 +/- 2 Hz; DEC-054's classes: mild 0.03-0.16 mm, moderate 0.16-0.51 mm, severe above 0.51 mm, typically 1.7 mm) and the population, never 'tremor' alone
rationale: The data's severe class starts at about 0.5 mm, far below the round-4 plan's 5-10 mm (its 0.3-1 / 2-4 / 5-10 mm classes are replaced by DEC-054). The classes are the median and 90th percentile of 24 tuning PD patients' tip tremor while drawing spirals, checked on 25 test patients (60/24/16 % against 50/40/10); they are a floor, since patients who could not draw on a tablet are missing (LIT PDT-82). This peak is zero-to-peak. EXP-H01 states peak-to-peak (A_pp = 2 sqrt(2) A_rms, human_study_plan.md s3.6), about twice as large for a steady tremor. REQ-USR-002 is now stated in this convention: 0.5 mm peak for full correction (it was 1 mm p-p), the lower edge of the severe class
source: DEC-054; docs/real_data.md (the tremor library); LIT PDT-75, PDT-82
verification: review of every claim; results cards (EXP-R02, AC-R02-04); the classes in writing (EXP-R01, AC-R01-02)
current_estimate: PD tip tremor while drawing is mostly 0.1-0.3 mm; severe (top 10 %) from 0.51 mm, representative 1.72 mm, largest test patient 7.1 mm (CALC on DATA, UCI spirals). No open recording of ET at the pen tip exists; ET waveforms from the hand are scaled to the PD classes (ASSUMPTION)

title: No non-causal inputs to controllers
requirement: Inputs built with non-causal (zero-phase) filters are never given to a controller or estimator; trackers see only the simulated or recorded sensor streams
rationale: The realdata library extracts each tremor waveform with zero-phase band limits (f0 +/- 2 Hz and 2 f0 +/- 2 Hz), which use the future of the recording; it drives the simulated hand only. This is the data-side complement of REQ-CTRL-009 (every command uses only samples available at its tick)
source: DEC-054; docs/real_data.md (the tremor library; how other studies use the library)
verification: code review; library docstrings; the pipeline check of EXP-R05 (AC-R05-02)
current_estimate: The library's docstrings mark every zero-phase filter as for inputs and statistics only, and the HW1 trackers saw only the simulated sensor streams (docs/real_data.md); no automated test checks it yet

title: Dataset licences
requirement: Datasets are used and redistributed only within their licences; results hold statistics only for research-only and non-commercial sources
rationale: UNIPEN (the iUF notice allows research use only; its Zenodo page tags CC BY 4.0, and the stricter terms apply), BRUSH (non-commercial research use), PADS (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0) and NewHandPD (no licence stated) restrict use; pictures of UNIPEN writing stay in realdata/build/figures_research_only/ (git-ignored). IAM-OnDB, PaHaW and OnHW need registration, an agreement or permission before use (EXP-R06)
verification: the source registry test (realdata/tests); EXP-R04 (AC-R04-01); EXP-R06 (AC-R06-01)
current_estimate: Every dataset used is in the registry with its licence and what may go into results/: statistics only for UNIPEN, BRUSH, PADS and NewHandPD; attributed excerpts for the CC BY sources (UCI, Zenodo); the registry test passes

title: Measured-error page sensor in every tracker simulation
requirement: Every simulation that reports tracker performance also reports it with a measured-error page-sensor model in the causal page model v2 (DEC-070: dropouts kept as lost motion, the absolute anchor invalid until restored; the DeltaPen-class error statistics for now, the model measured on paper by EXP-R07 once it exists); the ideal sensor and page model v1 only as labelled optimistic bounds
rationale: The independent review (R14) and DEC-054. Earlier tracker results assumed 1 kHz, 2 ms and 3 um of white noise (ASSUMPTION). The DeltaPen-class model gives all of DeltaPen's measured 10 ms window error (median 23.6 um, mean 68.3 um, on a Wacom surface, LIT OPT-02) to the sensor, so it is pessimistic. On paper the error is measured on rig R10 (EXP-T04, EXP-J10, DEC-059), and REQ-RVJ-C05 sets its limits. DEC-070 (the lead, 2026-09-30): the default page model is version 2; version 1 changed past readings when the future changed and recovered lost motion from the truth, so its results are suspended as device evidence until study X reruns them. Was (DEC-054): 'Every simulation that reports tracker performance also reports it with a measured-error page-sensor model (for now the DeltaPen-class model; the model measured on paper by EXP-R07 once it exists); the ideal sensor only as a labelled bound'
source: DEC-054; docs/real_data.md (the page sensor); LIT OPT-01, OPT-02
verification: results card with both columns (EXP-R02, AC-R02-05); EXP-R07 (AC-R07-01)
current_estimate: The DeltaPen-class model gives 27 um median and 76 um mean per 10 ms window on the tremor-free test notes (against 23.6 and 68.3); with it the results changed by at most 0.1 word and 0.01 mm against the ideal sensor (SIM). DEC-070: the DeltaPen-class figures used page model v1, which changed past readings and recovered lost motion from the truth; they stand only as labelled optimistic bounds, suspended as device evidence until study X reruns them with page model v2

title: Words read by a literal reader
requirement: Words-you-can-read results use a literal reader (no lexicon, no spelling correction, greedy decoding), and report the clean-ink ceiling of the same notes and a 95 % interval over writers
rationale: The independent review (s13) and DEC-054's results card. A reader with a lexicon or a correction step reads words that the ink does not show. The literal reader's decoder still has a language prior from its training text, so even clean notes are not all read: the ceiling row shows it. EXP-R03 checks the reader against people
current_estimate: TrOCR base, literal, chosen on the tuning notes: 6.8 of 10 words on the clean real test notes and 9.5 of 10 on synthetic notes (SIM)

title: Content of the EXP-H01 recordings
requirement: EXP-H01 recordings (with EXP-R01) hold ink on paper over a digitiser (>= 200 points/s, <= 0.05 mm, hover tracked), the pen's IMU with acquisition and availability time stamps, handedness, grip, posture, medication state and device configuration, and participant- and session-level splits
rationale: The independent review (s11) and the gaps of the open data: no open recording of ET at the pen tip; no dataset records availability times; patients' own writing (slower and smaller, adapted to their tremor) is missing from the composed inputs. R11's tablet protocol reports 0.01 mm but is accurate only to about +/-0.25 mm (LIT CON-101), so AC-H01-08 then registers the chain per stroke. It extends REQ-DATA-001 (splits by participant and session) to what the recordings hold
source: DEC-054; docs/real_data.md (proposed requirements); independent review 2026-09-29 s11
current_estimate: Not yet recorded. R11's tablet recorder logs every pen sample the browser receives, with time stamps (AC-T06-04 must show a median >= 200 Hz); the recording pen's IMU runs at 1.92 kHz (docs/measurement_rig.md s4.1)
