rationale: User request for an Apple-Pencil-class form factor (AMF-41: 8.9 x 166 mm, 19.15 g)
verification: EXP-M03 (mass and balance of built pens); EXP-H02 (form factor)
current_estimate: CAD 12.2 g before wiring and margin (Q layout); centre of mass 88 mm from the nib. Proposed P0.2 (DEC-030): 14.6 g including 10 % (CALC)

title: Writing force bypasses the nib
requirement: The user writing force is carried to the paper by a nose skid; the nib force is set by an axial spring at F_c <= 0.14 N (derived from REQ-PNC-003: the loaded stroke is +/-300 um at 0.14 N, +/-277 um at 0.15 N and about +/-180 um at 0.20 N, theta 50 deg, mu 0.15, worst stroke direction); EXP-Q02 shows whether an ink writes well at that force
rationale: Any transverse nib stage must hold N cos(theta) + friction (COR-01); no actuator that fits a 7.9 mm bore holds 0.76 N
verification: EXP-Q01 (skid friction); EXP-Q02 (low-force ink); EXP-Q06 (nib force behind the skid); EXP-H03 (skid feel)
current_estimate: Stage design load 0.170 N per axis behind the skid at the assumed F_c 0.15 N (just above the 0.14 N limit) vs 0.758 N with a conventional nib (docs/pencil_mechanisms.md s2)

title: Pencil stage stroke under load
requirement: Two-axis nib correction >= +/-0.30 mm under the design load over theta 35-75 deg, zero static hold power, first resonance >= 150 Hz
rationale: Tremor of 0.3 mm peak at the nib (REQ-ENV-003 nominal) must fit within the usable stroke
current_estimate: P0.1.2: +/-277 um at the design load (50 deg, nominal parts), 192 Hz; worst case (-20 % parts, 35 deg, mu 0.15, worst direction) 0 um (raw -67 um) under the hardware-study model. Proposed P0.2 (DEC-030): +/-477 um nominal (servo limit +/-300 um), worst case +/-212 um, 213 Hz (CALC, results/opt/hardware.json); still short of +/-0.30 mm in the worst corner, which needs F_c <= 0.10 N (EXP-Q02)

title: Page sensor for capture and guidance
requirement: Page-referenced position at >= 120 Hz with <= 10 ms latency, fused with the IMU between samples, inside the 8.9 mm nose
rationale: Guided mode loses most of its benefit at 30 Hz (0.76 of the no-correction error) and keeps it at >= 120 Hz (0.42)
verification: EXP-S01 on a candidate chip-scale sensor
current_estimate: No part found that fits and meets it (OPT-05 too large; OPT-36 30 fps). With the accelerometer tracker (DEC-025) 120 Hz / 10 ms costs little: tremor-band ratio 0.81 against 0.78 at 1 kHz (SIM); the frozen filter needed 1 kHz (0.998 at 120 Hz)

title: Pencil battery life
requirement: >= 2 h of assisted writing and >= 4 h of recording per charge
rationale: Liftware-class devices run about 1-1.5 h (ACT-16); a pencil used for notes needs a working session
verification: EXP-P01 (power and runtime); EXP-Q03 (cell pulse discharge); EXP-Q05 (driver efficiency)
current_estimate: P0.1.2: 90 mAh cell, recording 4.1 h; assist 0.50 h with 2 x DRV2700 and the real TMAG5170 Hall noise (2.3 um). Proposed P0.2 (DEC-030): assist 2.73 h in the worst 0.3 mm case with an LT8365 charge-recovery drive at 58 V and 2 x DRV5055A4 (CALC, results/opt/hardware.json)

title: Touchdown and lift tails
requirement: Extra ink at touchdown and lift, beyond what a rigid pen draws on the same writing, <= 0.1 mm per stroke; no missing ink
rationale: The skid architecture lets the ball slide up to 0.86 mm at every touchdown and lift with a tilt-range front stop, which harms legibility more than the tremor
current_estimate: Tail ink (within 30 ms of a touchdown or lift) with the tilt-adaptive stop at 0.31 mm and the touchdown feed-forward (DEC-026): 0.005 / 0.008 / 0.000 mm per stroke at 35 / 50 / 75 deg, no missing ink at the transitions (adaptive stop alone 0.14 / 0.11 / 0.00; tilt-range stop 0.35 / 0.81 / 0.42). Met in SIM for touchdown and lift; the all-extra-ink diagnostic (1.15 -> 0.33 -> 0.23 mm, 0.15 with the tuned servo) is dominated by the skid's in-stroke distortion, not the transitions. Open: 1.7 contact transitions per pen-down against 1.2 (short re-contacts after lift-off, bounce family of DEC-011)

title: Bounded guidance from predicted templates
requirement: Guidance toward any template is limited to the stage travel, scaled by the calibrated prediction confidence (ICD s5 rule 5), and must not make a written letter read as another letter in more than 1 % of letters when gated
rationale: Wrong predictions must not rewrite what the user writes
verification: EXP-A02; firmware tests of template rules T1-T8 (docs/ai_guidance.md s7.3)
current_estimate: Stage at its 0.40 mm stop at worst; 2.2 % of letters misread at full authority, 0.3 % gated (pencil model P1)

title: Autocorrect as a derived layer
requirement: Autocorrect changes only derived text layers that cite stroke ids; the original ink and base recognition layer are never modified; every change is visible and reversible; changes require posterior >= 0.9 by default; in the app a correction is only proposed: it changes the effective text only when the writer selects it, and a proposal made on an older or altered note is refused (DEC-074)
rationale: Immutable originals and provenance (DEC-017); names and rare words are the failure mode. DEC-074 (the lead, 2026-09-30): corrections are proposed, then explicitly accepted; propose_autocorrect changes nothing in storage, accept_autocorrect needs a selected proposal bound to the unchanged note and writes a user edit, keeping the original recognition and ink; the derived-layer autocorrect (autocorrect_note) stays as the evaluation API that EXP-A03 scores. Was: 'Autocorrect changes only derived text layers that cite stroke ids; the original ink and base recognition layer are never modified; every change is visible and reversible; changes require posterior >= 0.9 by default'
verification: app/tests/test_autocorrect.py (the proposal and acceptance tests, DEC-074); app/tests/test_cli.py; EXP-A03 on real notes (AC-A03-01)
current_estimate: Word errors 32 % -> 10 % at 7 % recognition errors; <= 0.1 % of correct words changed; names 6-14 % wrongly changed without a personal dictionary

title: Rev H envelope
requirement: Handle grip diameter <= 24 mm and length <= 175 mm; mass <= 80 g without the inertial module and <= 110 g with it
rationale: The user chose a bigger grip (DEC-029); Liftware-class handheld stabilisers weigh about 100 g (ACT-16); pen barrels of 13-21 mm were compared for grip kinetics (HAP-37)
current_estimate: Ø22 x 170 mm; 75.0 g, 103 g with the rear inertial module (92 g with a 10440 cell) (CALC, results/revH/tip_params.json)

title: Rev H tip travel
requirement: Ball travel relative to the handle >= +/-2.5 mm in every direction over theta 35-75 deg with the skid ring on the paper; cross-coupling between axes <= 10 %
rationale: Covers 1-2 mm hand tremor at the tip with margin; travel beyond +/-1.5 mm changed the causal result by < 0.03 in SIM, so +/-2.5 mm leaves room for guidance
current_estimate: +/-3.0 mm usable, 3.5 mm stop at 50 deg (PROPOSED DESIGN); front end closed over 35-75 deg: >= 2.75 mm in every direction with the nozzle >= 0.80 mm above the paper (CALC, DEC-034); never at the limit for 2 mm tremor with perfect knowledge except peaks at 10-12 Hz (SIM)

title: Rev H nose servo
requirement: Closed-loop nose bandwidth (-3 dB) >= 60 Hz with phase margin >= 45 deg, with the real Hall noise; nose force constant >= 0.40 N/sqrt(W) per axis at the magnets
rationale: The tremor band reaches 12 Hz; a servo above 80 Hz changed the causal result by < 0.03 in SIM
current_estimate: Km 0.47 N/sqrt(W) at the magnets (adjoint design); 80 Hz servo ASSUMPTION (CALC, SIM) CONTESTED by DEC-041: an image-method magnetics model gives 0.19 N/sqrt(W) at the magnets (study N, docs/nose_v2.md s4.2); measure first (EXP-N01, AC-N01-03).

title: Rev H power
requirement: Average power while writing <= 0.1 W without the inertial module (>= 20 h of writing per charge on a 750 mAh cell) and <= 0.15 W with it
rationale: All-day use without daily anxiety about charge; the skid carries the load, so the nose only steers
current_estimate: 0.081 W (about 27 h) without the module; module <= 0.051 W, worst case about 17 h (CALC on SIM forces) CONTESTED by DEC-041: with 0.19 N/sqrt(W) the coil loss while writing rises from about 0.004 W to 0.027 W (docs/nose_v2.md s4.2), close to the limit; measure first (EXP-N01).

title: Writing force undisturbed
requirement: Change of the writing (paper-normal) force caused by the nose <= 0.05 N rms while correcting 1 mm tremor
rationale: A tilting rigid nose presses the tip into the paper (architecture A: 0.31-0.71 N rms), which changes ink and feel
current_estimate: Architecture B: none by construction, the refill slides on its 0.15 N spring (SIM)

title: Tremor tracker on real writing
requirement: On recorded writing with 8-12 Hz tremor of >= 1 mm at the tip, ink-error ratio <= 0.8 against the pen with the nose held, with tremor-free writing moved <= 15 um RMS
rationale: The mechanism can remove 76-91 % of tremor up to 2 mm; the tracker decides how much the writer gets
current_estimate: 0.64 / 0.70 / 0.76 at r_rot 0.3 / 0.5 / 0.7 with 10-13 um false correction (SIM, synthetic writers); nothing at 4-6 Hz

title: Writer stays in charge
requirement: Neither the pen nor the board produces a stroke the writer did not start: nose authority scales with the tracker confidence and is limited to the travel; board force <= 0.4 N and it yields within 0.5 s when the writer resists; a stop is always available
rationale: Agency and safety; learning is shown only without guidance (HAP-01...06)
current_estimate: Board software cap 0.4 N; a determined wrong letter is not overpowered (SIM); nose authority gating by the tracker (DEC-025)

title: Refill front stop follows the nose
requirement: The Rev H refill's front stop follows the nose deflection, or allows at least the usable travel x cot(theta_min) + 0.3 mm of extension
rationale: Tilting the nose by q changes the ball's height by about q x z_p x cot(theta); with a fixed stop 0.3 mm beyond contact the ball touched the paper only 63-73 % of pen-down time under correction (sim2). A fixed long stop lets a free refill follow ordinary pen lifts (DEC-041 item 3), so that option also needs the pen lift or a refill lock
verification: CAD check; EXP-V02 part B; sim2 frontstop stage
current_estimate: Stop that follows the nose (sim2 default): ball in contact 0.908-1.000 of pen-down time, oracle ratio 0.095-0.282; fixed stop 3.2 mm beyond contact: 0.984-1.000, 0.109-0.336; fixed 0.3 mm stop: 0.63-0.73 (SIM, training seeds 300-301). Fixed margin needed: 2.8 mm at 50 deg, 4.6 mm at 35 deg for the 3.0 mm usable travel (CALC). No mechanism designed. DEC-070: the sim2 and sim2j figures here used the legacy ideal sensing (exact velocity, immediate true contact, a 400 Hz loop, page model v1), so they are upper bounds on performance (DEC-070's optimistic bounds), suspended as device evidence until study X reruns them
trace: DEC-041; results/sim2/verification.json frontstop; docs/sim_v2.md s5.8, s10

title: Heel force cap
requirement: The heel drive's commanded force stays at or below 0.5 N (software cap) and at or below 0.8 x the estimated traction (mu_hat x wheel load); the steered wheel's passive hold across its heading is capped at the same level by a lateral release (the excess turns the wheel toward the push); the physical limit is the static traction (about 0.36-0.73 N)
rationale: Handwriting-guidance devices used 0.43-0.49 N; the desk board 0.4 N; far below ISO/TS 15066 hand limits; the pen always yields to a writer who resists (Rev J envelope)
source: DEC-037; HAP-15; HAP-16; HAP-51; HAP-70; docs/grounded_drive.md s4.4
current_estimate: Commands capped in every SIM run; passive hold up to 0.66 N without the release (test, loops); 95th percentile 0.43-0.50 N and maximum 0.49-0.56 N with it (tuning writers after the test, mu 1.2)

title: The writer always wins
requirement: The drive yields (force to zero within 0.1 s) when the pen is held more than 4 mm off the template for 0.3 s, when the writer's grip force against the drive exceeds 0.5 N for 0.3 s, or on lift; it never keeps pushing against a stalled pen
rationale: Users resent tools that act against their intention; a writer set on 'b' must still write 'b'
source: DEC-037; HAP-22; HAP-23; HAP-62; SIM reversal (writer set on b: 0 % converted)
current_estimate: A writer set on 'b' kept 'b' under every device (push at most 0.37-0.47 N, felt change 0.34-0.48 N at the 95th percentile); the yield rule never had to act, also for a lightly resisting writer (SIM, docs/grounded_drive.md s5.2, s5.3)

title: Passive by default
requirement: In guidance and tremor modes the wheel is steered (and braked) only: it cannot move the pen on its own. The wheel is driven only in an explicit lead-through or autowrite mode the user turns on (DEC-039), and never starts a stroke
rationale: Cobot principle: steering channels the writer's own motion with almost no power (intrinsically passive); Rev J envelope: 'writes for you' only in an explicit mode
current_estimate: Met by the mode logic (SIM); the steer-only wheel drew none of a 'd' bowl with a relaxed hand (docs/grounded_drive.md s5.3)

title: Traction on paper
requirement: Tyre-paper kinetic friction >= 0.6 on the six reference papers at 0.3-0.6 N, dry and at 60 % RH; preload 0.55 N +/- 10 %
rationale: The usable force is mu x wheel load; rubber on paper is 1.05-2.2 for feed rollers, but paper friction tests reproduce only within 24-27 % between labs
current_estimate: Design range 0.6-1.2 (ASSUMPTION); the mean writer gets 0.30 N of traction at mu 0.6 and the weakest 10 % 0.21 N (CALC)

title: Slip detection
requirement: Gross wheel slip is detected within 50 ms (paper sensor against wheel odometry) and the command is lowered; false slip flags fewer than 1 per 10 s of writing
rationale: Slip wastes force and marks the paper; the SIM detector raises many false flags at mode switches. It depends on the page sensor staying in its lens band, which holds only within about +/-1.5 deg of pen roll (DEC-044, REQ-RVJ-N06)
source: DEC-037; AMF-109; SIM (slip flags against true sliding)
current_estimate: Tracing: true sliding < 0.1 % of contact time, yet 3-40 false flags per sentence with the simple rule (SIM); a model-based detector using the tyre deflection is needed. At risk when the pen is rolled, as REQ-RVJ-N06 (CALC, DEC-044); the wheel's odometry could bridge short dropouts

title: Steering speed
requirement: Steering servo bandwidth >= 40 Hz and rate >= 300 rad/s at the wheel
rationale: Letter headings turn at up to 71 rad/s (p90) and 283 rad/s (p99) on the synthetic writers
current_estimate: 0620 B + crown 2:1: about 1570 rad/s no-load at 3.7 V (CALC); SIM servo 40 Hz, limited to 500 rad/s (ASSUMPTION)

title: Roll and tilt tolerance
requirement: The wheel keeps contact over tilts 35-75 deg and pen roll +/-20 deg (spring travel >= 0.75 mm)
rationale: Writers roll the pen; the wheel sits at one azimuth of the heel. Was: spring travel >= 0.54 mm on the Rev H front end (study D); the Rev J ring (11.65 mm) needs 0.75 mm for +/-20 deg of roll (DEC-044)
current_estimate: Rev J (DEC-044): 0.75 mm of spring travel keeps contact to +/-20 deg of roll; the wheel reaches 0.32 / 0.22 / 0.18 mm below the ring's paper plane at 35 / 50 / 75 deg, so its 0.55 N preload always acts (CALC)

title: Front-end size and ink view
requirement: Heel (wheel) contact radius <= 12.0 mm and skid-ring contact radius <= 11.65 mm; front sleeve <= 23.3 mm, flush with the ring, and <= 24 mm where held; the ring stays open 120 deg on top, and the opening carries on 10 mm into the sleeve so the ink stays visible
rationale: The drive must sit outside the swinging nose; the Rev J envelope allows 24 mm where held. Was: heel contact radius <= 9.0 mm and front sleeve <= 18.5 mm at the heel, sized by study D on the Rev H front end; DEC-044 fits the heel to the nose v2 front end (the steering crown sets the 12.0 mm)
source: DEC-037; DEC-036; CALC drive/geometry.py; docs/revJ_plan.md s6
current_estimate: Met at the limits (DEC-044): wheel 12.0 mm, ring 11.65 mm, sleeve front 23.3 mm flush (Rev H's 0.75 mm step would make it 24.8 mm), 24 mm where held with 0.00 mm margin; the C opening carried 10 mm into the sleeve (CALC, PROPOSED DESIGN)
trace: DEC-037; DEC-036; DEC-044; revj/frontend.py; results/revJ/frontend.json; mechanics/cad/revJ_pen.py

title: Power and heat
requirement: Heel drive electrical power (motors and drivers) <= 0.15 W mean in any mode; winding rise < 10 K
rationale: Rev H uses about 0.08 W. The pen's hours per mode are REQ-RVJ-I01, and the page sensor's power is REQ-RVJ-I07 (DEC-045). Was: motors, drivers and paper sensor <= 0.15 W, and the pen still writes >= 8 h with assistance on (the 750 mAh cell must last a school day)
source: DEC-037; DEC-045; AMF-100; docs/revH_concept.md; docs/revJ1_design.md s4.7
current_estimate: Rev J.1 (DEC-045): heel drive 0-2 mW in the steady mode (drivers asleep), 11-26 mW guiding and 103-113 mW leading (84 mW SIM / 0.9 for the fourth gear mesh, plus 10-20 mW of motor drivers, ASSUMPTION); winding rise 5-11 K (CALC). With the PMW3610-class page sensor counted too, 0.105-0.115 W while leading

title: Noise
requirement: Drive noise <= 35 dB(A) at 30 cm while guiding (ASSUMPTION threshold, quiet classroom)
rationale: Two 6 mm motors and watch-scale gears may whine
current_estimate: Unknown (not modelled)

title: Paper must be held
requirement: Instructions and app state that the sheet must be held (other hand, clip or pad) whenever the drive pushes; the drive's force stays below the sheet's holding force
rationale: A loose sheet slides when the drive's reaction exceeds mu_paper-desk x the loads on it
current_estimate: A loose sheet under 1 N slides at 0.25-0.5 N; with the writing hand resting (1 N) and mu 0.5 it holds 1.0 N (CALC; paper-desk mu ASSUMPTION)

title: Clean and replaceable contact
requirement: The tyre and the heel pod can be cleaned or replaced by the user; the pod is sealed against paper dust and ink
rationale: Rolling contacts on paper jam with dust and eraser crumbs (prior art)
current_estimate: Not yet designed or tested

title: Zero force in the air
requirement: Drive torque goes to zero within 20 ms when the wheel load falls below 0.02 N (pen lift); the wheel is pre-steered during lifts
rationale: Pen-up gaps: nothing to push against; dysgraphic writers stop and lift more often
current_estimate: Met in SIM

title: End-cap envelope
requirement: Bench only (DEC-051: no end-cap in the product; it stays a bench comparison against the same mass locked): the end-cap module is <= 26 mm across and <= 45 mm long, <= 45 g, <= 1 W peak and <= 0.3 W average, and the Rev J.1 pen with it fitted stays <= 175 mm and <= 120 g, so that the bench result stands for a module that could be fitted
rationale: Rev J envelope (lead): the pen <= 120 g with every module; a heavier or hungrier end-cap costs grip comfort and battery. Was: the base pen <= 120 g and the pen with the end-cap fitted <= 130 g (provisional; DEC-044 gave 129.2 g with the 43.3 g end-cap); DEC-045's 29.6 g end-cap meets the envelope. Was (DEC-045), a product requirement: 'Rear end-cap <= 26 mm across and <= 45 mm long, <= 45 g, <= 1 W peak and <= 0.3 W average; the pen stays <= 175 mm and <= 120 g with the end-cap fitted'
verification: CAD check; weighing (EXP-K01); EXP-K01 power log; EXP-J09 (acceptance of the masses)
current_estimate: Rev J.1 (DEC-045): end-cap Ø26 x 21 mm, 29.6 g (9 mm tungsten slug, 17.3 g); 0.082 W average in the design model and 0.028 W in the SIM test runs (peak not recomputed; study K's 45 g end-cap 1.0 W). Pen 143.9 mm and 84.3 g base; 161.9 mm and 112.7 g with the end-cap, centre of mass 102.5 mm from the tip (CALC): 7.3 g under 120 g
trace: DEC-038; DEC-044; DEC-045; results/endcap/endcap_study.json; results/revJ1/budgets.json; results/revJ1/endcap.json

title: End-cap tremor benefit
requirement: Bench only (DEC-051): with the nose on, on a hand simulant, the end-cap adds >= 10 % further reduction of the ink error at 8-12 Hz and 1-2 mm at the measured grip split (>= 5 % at the other splits) and never raises it on average; a return to the product is judged by REQ-WP-001
rationale: Pre-declared rule R-T1 of study K; same bar as DEC-033 for the Rev H module. Was (DEC-038), a product requirement: 'With the nose on, on a hand simulant, the end-cap adds >= 10 % further reduction of the ink error at 8-12 Hz and 1-2 mm at the measured grip split (>= 5 % at the other splits) and never raises it on average'. Product entry for any added device is now REQ-WP-001 (>= 10 % against the same pen with the device locked, at three grip strengths, coverage kept)
source: DEC-038; DEC-051; DEC-033; study K rule R-T1
verification: EXP-K02 (with EXP-I06); EXP-J16 (the Rev J.1 end-cap); EXP-T16 (rig R14, three grip strengths)
current_estimate: +8 / +18 / +20 % at r_rot 0.3 / 0.5 / 0.7 on top of the Rev H nose (seed spread +4 to +25 %); no split worse on average (SIM, H1, synthetic writers, test seeds 200-203); not re-run with nose v2. Rev J.1 end-cap (29.6 g, DEC-045): +5.6 / +16.8 / +18.3 % (SIM, same model and test seeds; rule R-T1 passes by 0.6 points at 0.3)

title: Active beats its own weight
requirement: Bench only (DEC-051): on the bench the active end-cap is compared with the same mass fixed in the end-cap and must beat it by >= 5 points of further reduction at the measured grip split; the product fits neither, and a return is judged by REQ-WP-001
rationale: The weight alone gives part of the benefit in SIM; an active part costs power and complexity. Was (DEC-038), a product requirement: 'An active end-cap is fitted only if it beats the same mass fixed in the end-cap by >= 5 points of further reduction at the measured grip split; otherwise fit the weight or nothing'. REQ-WP-001's gate (>= 10 % over the device locked, at every grip strength, coverage kept) is stricter; AC-T16-01, which asked it as a hypothesis on this requirement, is now REQ-WP-001's criterion
verification: EXP-K02; EXP-K03; EXP-J16; EXP-T16 (rig R14, three grip strengths)
current_estimate: The same 45 g fixed: +17 / +12 / +4 %, so the motion adds -9 / +6 / +16 points at r_rot 0.3 / 0.5 / 0.7; the fixed weight makes 8 / 29 / 42 % of the hard cases worse than the nose alone, the moving slug 4 / 12 / 4 % (SIM). Rev J.1 end-cap (29.6 g, DEC-045): the same mass fixed +12.6 / +11.1 / +6.7 %, so the motion adds -7.0 / +5.7 / +11.6 points (SIM)

title: No writing claim for inertia
requirement: Superseded for the product by DEC-051: the pen carries no end-cap. If one returns through REQ-WP-001, no product text, mode or app screen may claim that it moves, steers or writes letters; it is described as a steadier and a cue
rationale: SIM: no end-cap design reaches the 2 mm 'can write' line at 1-3 Hz. Was (DEC-038), a product requirement: 'No product text, mode or app screen may claim that the end-cap moves, steers or writes letters; the end-cap is described as a steadier and a cue'
source: DEC-038; DEC-051; study K s6 (rule R-S1)
current_estimate: Largest ink shift at 1-3 Hz: reaction mass 0.21 mm, CMG 1.06 mm, against 2 mm to write (SIM)

title: Cue side effect
requirement: Superseded for the product by DEC-051: the pen carries no end-cap. If one returns through REQ-WP-001, any end-cap cue given while the ball is on the paper keeps the ink jitter <= 30 um RMS; otherwise cues are given only in pauses or with the pen lifted
rationale: Pre-declared rule R-C1; a cue that moves the ink defeats the pen. Was (DEC-038), a product requirement: 'Any end-cap cue given while the ball is on the paper keeps the ink jitter <= 30 um RMS; otherwise cues are given only in pauses or with the pen lifted'. The pen's cue is now an LRA tick (DEC-056; EXP-S13)
source: DEC-038; DEC-051; study K s8 (rule R-C1)
current_estimate: A 0.5 N, 40 + 80 Hz cue moves the ink 186 um RMS while writing (116-239 um over the grip splits); 76 um at 0.25 N; 31 um at 75 Hz (SIM): cues belong in pauses

title: Cue validated in the target users
requirement: Superseded for the product by DEC-051: the pen carries no end-cap. If one returns through REQ-WP-001, a directional end-cap cue is shipped only if >= 90 % of directions are named correctly by writers with ET and with PD (with tremor) in EXP-K05
rationale: Pseudo-force direction was near chance on sides with tremor in the only patient study found (preprint). Was (DEC-038), a product requirement: 'A directional cue is shipped only if >= 90 % of directions are named correctly by writers with ET and with PD (with tremor) in EXP-K05'
current_estimate: Healthy adults 93-99 % (HAP-82, HAP-84, HAP-85); tremor sides near chance (PDT-39, preprint)

title: Rotor safety (only if a rotor is fitted)
requirement: Applies to the CMG research module (no rotor in the product, DEC-038): stored rotor energy <= 3 J; a burst is contained by the end-cap; the rotor stops within 2 s after a fall is detected; balance grade G1 or better (G0.4 is the gyroscope class); spin-up <= 10 s
rationale: A spinning tungsten disc in a hand-held pen is a new hazard (Rev J plan s6). REQ-WP-010 (DEC-051) asks more of any gyroscope in the tail tests (EXP-W14): <= 2 J and a burst excluded by design (stress margin >= 3, over-speed trip); this requirement keeps its lines for the end-cap's CMG research module
current_estimate: CMG end-cap: 3.0 J (at the cap), spin-up 8.1 s, 466 Hz tone, centre stress 3.9 MPa against >= 724 MPa (factor 184), imbalance 0.16 N at G2.5 and 0.026 N at G0.4 (CALC); stop time 2 s is a target (ASSUMPTION)

title: Battery with the end-cap
requirement: Superseded for the product by DEC-051: the pen carries no end-cap, so REQ-RVJ-I01 has no end-cap row. If one returns through REQ-WP-001: with it fitted and active only while a tremor line is detected, >= 8 h of steady writing up to 1 mm tremor at the end-cap's measured duty and >= 6 h at its design power
rationale: One set of battery targets for every mode (docs/revJ1_design.md s4.7); the id is kept so that references still resolve. Was: >= 8 h of writing per charge with the end-cap active (Rev J envelope). Was (DEC-045): 'Folded into REQ-RVJ-I01 by DEC-045 as its end-cap row: with the end-cap fitted and active only while a tremor line is detected, >= 8 h of steady writing up to 1 mm tremor at the end-cap's measured duty and >= 6 h at its design power'
source: DEC-038; DEC-051; DEC-045; docs/revJ_plan.md s6; docs/revJ1_design.md s4.7
verification: EXP-K01 power log with the nose on (AC-K01-05)
current_estimate: Rev J.1 (DEC-045), steady writing at 1 mm tremor with the end-cap active: 7.7-8.6 h at the end-cap's SIM power (27.6 mW; 8.6 h only with the typical electronics) and 6.4-7.1 h at its design power (82 mW) (CALC, SIM). Rev J (DEC-044): 4.3-6.6 h

title: Non-magnetic mass near the sensors
requirement: Tungsten parts within 20 mm of a Hall sensor or coil are a non-magnetic grade (W-Ni-Cu class)
rationale: W-Ni-Fe heavy alloys are weakly ferromagnetic and would bias the Hall sensors and the coils
current_estimate: ET95NM relative permeability <= 1.05 (AMF-49); INERMET grades paramagnetic (AMF-125)

title: Guaranteed tip travel
requirement: Bench research module only (DEC-050: the C1S nose is not carried forward into Rev K; it stays for autowrite research): ball travel relative to the handle >= 6.0 mm in every direction over 35-75 deg of tilt with the skid ring on the paper. The product's nib travel is REQ-BNIB-003 (+/-1.0 mm)
rationale: Autowrite of 2.5 mm letters needs 4.1 mm for the worst tuning writer, plus 1 mm kept free for tremor (CALC, docs/nose_v2.md s2); also covers 3 mm letters; the 100 ms of delayed ink it also allowed for was dropped by DEC-042. Was (DEC-036, DEC-044, DEC-045), a product requirement: 'Ball travel relative to the handle >= 6.0 mm in every direction over 35-75 deg of tilt with the skid ring on the paper'
current_estimate: Rev J integrated layout (DEC-044): 6.00 mm guaranteed and 6.57 mm nominal at 50 deg (nose angle raised to 0.0859 rad so that the larger heel ring keeps 6.0 mm at 75 deg); skid ring 11.65 mm, heel wheel 12.0 mm; refill slide 26.6 mm (CALC)

title: Nose force and bandwidth
requirement: Bench research module only (DEC-050: the C1S nose is not carried forward into Rev K; it stays for autowrite research): the C1S nose's force constant at the tip >= 0.85 x the design value (0.099 N/sqrt(W) per axis, so >= 0.084) over the whole travel; closed-loop bandwidth >= 60 Hz; first parasitic mode >= 240 Hz. For the product nib B1: REQ-BNIB-006 (modes and bandwidth) and REQ-BNIB-003 (travel sized at Km x 0.7)
rationale: The design's power and heat margins rest on Km; the magnetics are an upper bound (image method, CALC, docs/nose_v2.md s4.2); 240 Hz is 3 x the 80 Hz servo. Was (DEC-036, DEC-044, DEC-045), a product requirement: 'Force constant at the tip >= 0.85 x the design value (0.099 N/sqrt(W) per axis, so >= 0.084) over the whole travel; closed-loop bandwidth >= 60 Hz; first parasitic mode >= 240 Hz'
verification: EXP-N01; EXP-N03 (the C1S module); EXP-T08 (AC-T08-03, a magnet-loaded suspension); B1's coupon and nib are judged by REQ-BNIB-003 and 006 in EXP-T07 and T10
current_estimate: 0.66 N/sqrt(W) at the magnets, 0.099 N/sqrt(W) at the tip (image-method magnetics, an upper bound); first parasitic mode 788 Hz; 80 Hz servo used in SIM (CALC)

title: Heat
requirement: Bench research module only (DEC-050: the C1S nose is not carried forward into Rev K; it stays for autowrite research): while autowriting with 1 mm tremor for 30 min the coil temperature rise is <= 20 K, and held surfaces stay <= 43 C absolute in a rated 30 C room (a 13 K rise), with 41 C as the design target, checked at the web over the coil plate (the rule of REQ-THM-001). The product's rules are REQ-THM-001 and B1's REQ-BNIB-010
rationale: Skin contact: ECMA-287 Table 5.2 gives 43 C for continuously held parts, and its B.5 lets the maker rate a warmer room (LIT AMF-35); under IEC 60601-1, 41 C needs no justification (LIT AMF-34). With 2 mm tremor the coil loss doubles, so such texts must stay short. Was: 'skin surface <= 41 C at the web over the coil plate in a 30 C room' (DEC-044); before that 'grip surface <= 41 C' with no room named. Was (DEC-036, DEC-044, DEC-045), a product requirement: 'Coil temperature rise <= 20 K while autowriting with 1 mm tremor for 30 min; held surfaces <= 43 C absolute in a rated 30 C room (a 13 K rise), with 41 C as the design target, checked at the web over the coil plate (the rule of REQ-THM-001)'
verification: EXP-N04; EXP-J05; EXP-J13 (the C1S module); B1's heat is REQ-BNIB-010 in EXP-T15
current_estimate: Rev J.1 (DEC-045), 0.1 mm graphite sheet in the shell wall (+0.21 g): the web 35.9 C at 1 mm tremor in a 30 C room, coil rise 8.5-8.7 K; autowrite with 2 mm tremor 43.7 C and 20.0 K: short texts, or a firmware cap at 0.39 W of coil loss (the coils may dissipate 0.395 W for 43 C and 0.334 W for 41 C) (CALC, fin model). At 2 x study N's coil power the web reaches 42.1 C at 1 mm tremor, at 5 x 63.8 C. Suspended by DEC-046 until study B and EXP-J17: with the refill spring's static side load (1.6 W at 50 deg, REQ-RVJ-N10) the coil would settle 162 K above the room, and at sim2's 2.68 W on the paper it passes 120 C after about 22 s (CALC on SIM; 100 K/W and 0.5 J/K ASSUMPTION). title: Pen lift
requirement: Bench research module only (DEC-050: the C1S nose is not carried forward into Rev K; it stays for autowrite research): the C1S module's pen lift raises the ball >= 0.3 mm off the paper and lowers it within 8 ms of the command, holds either state with no power, >= 1e7 cycles. Rev K keeps a pen lift (DEC-050, DEC-064): the follower of the counter-face head pulls the head back and lifts the ball 0.5 mm off the paper with no holding energy; DEC-064 is revisited if a lift takes longer than 0.25 s or a positioner back-drives under 0.2 N; its life is set with the build
rationale: Strokes stay separate at 50-70 deg (a free refill follows ordinary pen lifts, DEC-041 item 3); autowrite and delayed ink need it (docs/nose_v2.md s2, s5). Was (DEC-036, DEC-044, DEC-045), a product requirement: 'The pen lifts the ball >= 0.3 mm off the paper and lowers it within 8 ms of the command, holds either state with no power, >= 1e7 cycles'. The spelling cue's lift (DEC-056 (d)) and the write-only-when-in-reach gate (EXP-W16) need one on Rev K, so DEC-050 keeps one. DEC-064 (2026-09-30): the follower's lift serves the spelling cue (EXP-S12/S18); a gated mode (EXP-W16) needs a faster lift (a latching lift coil on the float, not designed). Rev K's sentence was: 'Rev K keeps a pen lift (DEC-050): the counter-face's follower-stop screw is the first candidate to lift the refill about 0.5 mm; its speed, holding and life are set with the Rev K layout'
verification: EXP-N05 (the C1S module); B1's lifts are judged in EXP-T11 (AC-T11-03, REQ-BNIB-002); Rev K's pen lift: EXP-K23 (AC-K23-01, the lift time; AC-K23-02, the positioners' holding), used by EXP-S12/S18; EXP-W16's gated mode needs a faster lift (DEC-064)
current_estimate: Rev K (DEC-064, CALC; the SQL-RV-1.8's speed-force line ASSUMPTION between MFR points): 0.5 mm at the ball, up in 0.155-0.18 s and down in 0.08-0.14 s, 0.08-0.31 J per lift, no holding energy; too slow for a gated mode, for which a latching lift coil on the float (8 ms, not designed) is the option. The C1S module: 0.5 mm lift, 5 ms switching (8 ms command to contact in SIM), 17 mJ per cycle, 0.07 W while autowriting, no holding power (electro-permanent brake and bistable latch) (CALC on ASSUMPTION inputs); freedom-to-operate review of PAT-01 open

title: Refill force element
requirement: Superseded for the product by DEC-050 (the refill spring force is frozen only after gate G1: REQ-BNIB-014 and REQ-BNIB-008); kept for the C1S bench research module: ink force along the refill 0.15 N +/- 20 % over the whole refill slide (26.6 mm; tendon travel 27.4 mm), never above 0.2 N along the refill; no fatigue failure within 1e8 small cycles
rationale: Stock constant-force springs are rated 2 500-25 000 cycles (MFR AMF-144); tremor stabilisation cycles the slide about 29 000 times per hour; the ball's drag is the nose's largest load. The slide was 24.4 mm with study N's front end; DEC-044's larger ring makes it 26.6 mm. Was (DEC-036, DEC-044, DEC-045), a product requirement: 'Ink force along the refill 0.15 N +/- 20 % over the whole refill slide (26.6 mm; tendon travel 27.4 mm), never above 0.2 N along the refill; no fatigue failure within 1e8 small cycles'
verification: EXP-N06; EXP-J06 (the C1S module); the lowest reliable ink force is REQ-BNIB-014 in EXP-T02
current_estimate: Rev J (DEC-044): spiral spring of 301 full-hard strip, 38 um x 2.6 x 139 mm, in the drum: 0.12-0.18 N along the refill over the 27.4 mm tendon travel, 0.19-0.21 N normal at the ball; Goodman safety factor 1.73 at 1e8 small cycles (+/-1.3 mm) and 1.30 at full travel (CALC; fatigue strength LIT AMF-20 with 0.8 ASSUMPTION); a 0.3 N ink force raised the coil loss 2.4-fold (SIM)

title: Page sensor
requirement: Handle position on the page at >= 1 kHz, <= 2 ms latency, <= 10 um rms, while writing at 35-75 deg of tilt and pen roll +/-20 deg, with the lens height within the sensor's working band
rationale: Autowrite's estimator and the SIM results assume it; with a 120 Hz, 10 ms sensor the autowrite ink error more than doubles (72 against 30 um); the heel drive uses it to detect slip (DEC-037). Was: 35-75 deg of tilt, no roll range named; writers roll the pen (REQ-DRV-007: +/-20 deg). DEC-050 keeps the page sensor in Rev K; REQ-BNIB-017 adds its lift range (the page kept through the lifts between strokes). In Rev K (DEC-062) the page sensor sits at the bottom of the 6.0 mm skid ring, the only place where it meets +/-20 deg of roll (its lens stays in the band up to 21 deg); the heel module's pod takes that place and leaves it 0.5 deg (fit check V1), so the heel module goes into a pen only if EXP-T04 finds a sensor that tolerates +/-20 deg of roll beside the pod (DEC-065)
verification: EXP-N07; EXP-J04; EXP-J10; EXP-T04 and EXP-T05 (rig R10, the bare sensor); Rev K: EXP-T04 (AC-T04-01; AC-T04-08, beside the heel module's pod)
current_estimate: Rev K (DEC-062, CALC): at the bottom of the ring the lens stays 2.22-2.42 mm above the paper with no roll and 2.22-2.58 mm at +/-20 deg of roll, inside the 2.2-2.6 mm band up to 21 deg; beside the heel module's pod it tolerates 0.5 deg. Rev J (DEC-044): folded optics beside the heel wheel; lens 2.23-2.45 mm above the paper over 35-75 deg with no roll, inside the 2.2-2.6 mm band (MFR OPT-54); 2.06-2.74 mm at +/-5 deg and 1.59-4.11 mm at +/-20 deg of roll, so the band holds only within about +/-1.5 deg (CALC): at risk. SIM assumed 1 kHz, 2 ms, 3 um noise; no part tested. Rev J.1 (DEC-045): a PMW3610-class die in the same place and optics, on in every mode; its frame rate and accuracy on paper are not stated (MFR OPT-61): EXP-J10; a PMW3360-class die stays the fallback for autowrite

title: Autowrite is a mode the user turns on
requirement: Bench research mode with the C1S nose, with no executable claim (DEC-050: autowrite needs about +/-4-6 mm of reach, which the product's B1 nib does not have; DEC-071: in-pen autowrite of whole accepted words is superseded as an executable claim): The pen draws letters on its own only in an explicit autowrite mode the user turns on, and only text the user accepted (typed, dictated, copied in the app, or a suggestion accepted with one action; DEC-049, DEC-056), in the user's own style, at up to 3 mm of tremor (DEC-049; sim2's peak at the hand); the app and the stroke record label that text as pen-written; it writes through a plan that starts a letter only when all of it fits within reach (REQ-CTRL-014); it follows the user's sweep and waits when the user slows; it sets the sweep speed per line and cues the user; it lifts the ball and stops drawing when the text leaves its reach; it never pushes the hand with the nose (the heel drive may lead a relaxed hand at gross scale, DEC-037); assistance modes never start a stroke
rationale: docs/revJ_plan.md s6; HAP-62 (users were frustrated when a handheld robot disobeyed); ACT-100 (Origin retracts when out of bounds). Amends REQ-RVH-007 for this mode (DEC-039). DEC-049 widens the mode to accepted text (study S's accepted suggestions) and to 3 mm of tremor, with the text labelled pen-written; DEC-056 (f) feeds it through the writing plan with letter admission and a reach gate (REQ-CTRL-014). At 3 mm peak at the hand the ordinary pen's ink error was 1.38-1.55 mm rms (sim2), DEC-054's severe class at the tip. Was (DEC-039): 'The pen draws letters on its own only in an explicit autowrite mode the user turns on, and only a known text (typed, dictated or copied in the app) in the user's own style; it follows the user's sweep and waits when the user slows; it sets the sweep speed per line and cues the user; it lifts the ball and stops drawing when the text leaves its reach; it never pushes the hand with the nose (the heel drive may lead a relaxed hand at gross scale, DEC-037); assistance modes never start a stroke'. DEC-050 (2026-09-30) makes autowrite a bench research mode with the C1S nose until a low-power large-reach design exists; the text after the prefix is unchanged. DEC-071 (2026-09-30): in-pen autowrite of whole accepted words is superseded as an executable claim, so this requirement governs only the C1S research mode; whole words go to a grounded stage or a moving page (EXP-BB07, EXP-PL05). DEC-074: the text the pen writes is only a revision the user explicitly accepted, and a supervisor stops execution on stale sensing, lost anchoring, tracking, current or temperature limits. The prefix was: 'Bench research mode with the C1S nose (DEC-050: autowrite needs about +/-4-6 mm of reach, which the product's B1 nib does not have)'
verification: design review; EXP-N09 (AC-N09-02); EXP-S19 (the plan on the bench); EXP-S18 (accepted suggestions, one action)
current_estimate: In SIM the pen followed the sweep and waited: an uneven sweep (+/-30 %) or a drifting hand (+/-1 mm) left the ink at 30-31 um; one of six test writers needed a slower sweep for its line (post hoc) (docs/nose_v2.md s5.3, s5.5). DEC-049 (sim2, 6 test writers, 3 mm peak at the hand, 5 and 8 Hz): letters read 82 / 88 %, words (after autocorrect) 80 / 97 %, ink 67 / 83 um from the planned letters; the nose used 6.55 of its 6.57 mm. Study S (kinematics only): an accepted word at a 3 mm x-height is written in full in 95 % of cases at +/-6 mm with the hand advancing, 23 % at +/-4 mm, 2 % with a still hand. DEC-070: the sim2 and sim2j figures here used the legacy ideal sensing (exact velocity, immediate true contact, a 400 Hz loop, page model v1), so they are upper bounds on performance (DEC-070's optimistic bounds), suspended as device evidence until study X reruns them

The prefix was: 'Bench research mode with the C1S nose (DEC-050: autowrite needs about +/-4-6 mm of reach, which the product's B1 nib does not have)'

title: Front stop
requirement: Bench research module only (DEC-050: the C1S nose is not carried forward into Rev K; it stays for autowrite research): the C1S module's refill front stop engages within 0.3 mm of slide beyond the ball's contact position, and the ink tail after a 30 mm/s pen lift is <= 0.5 mm. In Rev K the float of the counter-face head limits the refill to 1.0 mm beyond its writing position at 35 deg (0.6 mm at 75 deg) without a float brake, or 0.25 mm with one (REQ-BNIB-002, DEC-064)
rationale: With a fixed stop 0.3 mm beyond contact the ball touched the paper for only 63-73 % of pen-down time under correction (sim2, REQ-RVH-008), and a longer fixed stop lets a free refill follow ordinary pen lifts (DEC-041 item 3). REQ-RVH-008 covers Rev H; this is the Rev J rule, a stop that follows the nose (the drum brake). Was (DEC-036, DEC-044, DEC-045), a product requirement: 'The refill's front stop engages within 0.3 mm of slide beyond the ball's contact position, and the ink tail after a 30 mm/s pen lift is <= 0.5 mm'. The 0.5 mm ink-tail line stays for the B1 nib as a derived check in EXP-T11 (AC-T11-03). DEC-064 (2026-09-30) gives the face a float of +/-0.56 mm in place of study B's 0.25 mm gap to the follower stop; the old Rev K sentence was 'In Rev K the counter-face's follower stop limits the refill to 0.25 mm beyond its writing position (REQ-BNIB-002)'. Study K's ink tail after a natural lift is 0.28-1.1 mm without the brake (CALC), so AC-T11-03's 0.5 mm is at risk
source: DEC-041 item 4; DEC-044; DEC-045; DEC-050; docs/revJ_design.md s5.3; DEC-064
current_estimate: The drum brake locks when the slide runs 0.3 mm past the contact computed from the tilt and the nose position; at a 30 mm/s lift detection takes 7.7 ms and the brake 3 ms (ASSUMPTION): about 0.33 mm of ink tail; a 0.5 deg tilt error moves the computed contact by 0.17 mm (CALC; Rev J design, not changed by Rev J.1)

title: Static side load of the ball
requirement: With the refill spring at its nominal force and the ball on the paper at 35-75 deg of tilt, the nose's steady coil heat is <= 0.1 W
rationale: The spring presses the ball on the paper, and at tilt theta the paper pushes back sideways with F_c cot(theta). The soft C1S gimbal (2.8 mN m/rad) leaves that load to the coils on an 11.5 mm magnet arm: at 1.62 W the coil settles 162 K above the room, and at sim2's 2.68 W on the paper it passes 120 C after about 22 s (CALC on SIM; 100 K/W and 0.5 J/K ASSUMPTION). Rev H's 34 mm arm needs about 0.13 W for the same load (CALC). The 0.1 W target is an ASSUMPTION

The same nib unbalanced holds 314 mW at 35 deg. title: Nib suspension axial load
requirement: Rev K (DEC-050: the B1 nib replaces the C1S nose): the nib's suspension carries >= 2 x the measured axial magnetic force on its moving part without buckling, and axial stops keep it elastic after a 1 m drop; in B1 the magnets and keeper are handle-fixed and the coils move, so no actuator magnet rides on the suspension, and the wires' fatigue and drop are also REQ-BNIB-007 and REQ-BNIB-012. The C1S bench research module keeps the gimbal rule: the gimbal carries >= 2 x the measured axial magnetic pull of the actuator without buckling; its strips keep a fatigue safety factor >= 1.5 at full-travel tilt under the measured pull; axial stops keep the strips elastic after a 1 m drop; the spheres' centre sits on the pivot within 0.05 mm, axially and sideways
rationale: The magnet cap pulls toward the coil plate's iron with 12.4-22.2 N (ideal iron, by where the iron face is taken); study N's 50 um strips buckle at 16.4 N in compression (a co-rotational beam model; safety factor about 1.0, not the 1.24 of DEC-044), and a tail-first drop loads them further; an off-centre sphere adds negative stiffness or a steady torque the coils must hold. Was (DEC-044): >= 2 x the pull and the centring only. Re-scoped for Rev K (DEC-050): B1's moving coil puts no pull on its suspension, and the keeper's pull (9.1 N, CALC) acts between two handle-fixed parts; B1's four wires buckle sideways at 0.08 N in compression (CALC, docs/balanced_nib.md s5.2), so any axial force on the carrier, such as on the position sensor's 1 mm magnet, must stay well below that. Before the re-scope the requirement was the gimbal rule alone (DEC-044, DEC-045), now the C1S module's clause, unchanged; the title was 'Gimbal axial load'
source: DEC-044; DEC-045; docs/revJ1_design.md s3; AMF-20; DEC-050; docs/balanced_nib.md (s5.2)
verification: Rev K: EXP-T08 on the B1 coupon (AC-T08-04, the axial force on the carrier against the wires' buckling; AC-T08-01, the keeper pull) and EXP-B25 (the wires' stiffness, fatigue and drops); the C1S module: EXP-J01 (pull, centring); EXP-J11 (buckling, fatigue, drops); EXP-T08 (rig R12: suspension stiffness against the negative magnetic stiffness, AC-T08-02)
current_estimate: Rev K, B1 (CALC, docs/balanced_nib.md s5.2): no actuator magnet on the moving part; the keeper's pull 9.1 N between handle-fixed parts; the four wires buckle sideways at 0.08 N in compression, and behind 20 um axial stops they stay elastic in 500 and 2000 g drops; the force on the position sensor's magnet was not computed. The C1S module (values from the Rev J.1 layout; Rev K's layout is still to be done): Rev J.1 (DEC-045): 75 um x 2.55 x 3.8 mm 301 full-hard strips in compression, crossing at mid-length: buckling 55.3 N; Goodman safety factor 2.0 at 16.5 N and 1.7 at 22.2 N (1.0 at the crude 36 N); stiffness 9.4 mN m/rad unloaded and 22.7 at 16.5 N; a tail-first drop buckles the pivot above 222 g, and buckled strips stay elastic if the rear stop engages within 5 um (front stop within 20 um; stops not yet designed); an offset of 0.05 mm changes the stiffness by 3.6 % (axially) or costs 12 mW of holding power (sideways) (CALC). Strips in tension fail fatigue, and thrust pivots add 65-97 mN of friction at the ball (CALC)

title: Heel-motor cogging
requirement: The detent torque that the pen's magnets add at each heel motor is <= the motor's friction torque (0.011 mN m, MFR AMF-100); in Rev K the magnets are B1's pole magnets and keeper (DEC-050)
rationale: The heel motors sit under the cell near the C1S magnet cap (DEC-044: front faces 2.7 mm behind the coil plate; DEC-045 moves them and their gears 10 mm further back); a detent adds a once-per-turn force at the tyre (0.12 N at Rev J's place, against a 0.03 N backdrive). Re-scoped for Rev K (DEC-050): B1's four N52 poles (5.12 x 5.12 x 3.50 mm) and a 1010 keeper replace the C1S cap, and the heel wheel stays in Rev K, retracted by default (DEC-048). Until the Rev K layout exists, the estimate comes from the Rev J.1 layout (the C1S cap, with the motors 10 mm further back than Rev J's)
verification: EXP-J02 (the C1S cap at the Rev J.1 place); the same test with B1's magnets at Rev K's motor place once its layout exists
current_estimate: From the Rev J.1 layout (the C1S cap) until the Rev K layout exists: Rev J.1 (DEC-045), motors 10 mm further back: 0.0073 mN m, 0.66 x the friction torque (free space, an upper bound: the plate's back iron lies between; the black-anodised aluminium housing does not shield, MFR AMF-155); 0.062 mN m at Rev J's place (Rev J's 0.080 bound counted the axial field too) (CALC); a soft-iron cup does not fit

title: Nib position sensing near the magnets
requirement: Nib position error <= 10 um rms at the tip over the servo band, including the running heel motors, the pen lift and the coil currents (Rev K: B1's 3-D Hall sensor, whose own noise limit is REQ-BNIB-009; the C1S bench research module: its two linear Hall sensors)
rationale: The two linear Hall sensors (DRV5055-A4) on the main board sit among the actuator magnets, the heel motors and the pen-lift brake (DEC-044). Re-scoped for Rev K (DEC-050). Was (DEC-044): 'Nose position error <= 10 um rms at the tip over the servo band, including the running heel motors, the pen-lift brake and the coil currents'; the title was 'Nose position sensing near the magnets'. Until the Rev K layout exists, the heel motors' ripple and the Earth's-field figures come from the Rev J.1 layout (the DRV5055 pair on the main board)
verification: Rev K: EXP-T09 (rig R12: B1's sensor with the coils driven by linear and PWM drive, AC-T09-01 and AC-T09-03), then EXP-J03's test on Rev K's layout once it exists; the C1S module: EXP-J03; EXP-J02 (the motors' stray field)
current_estimate: Rev K, B1 (CALC, study B): 0.99 um rms at 1 kHz from the 3-D Hall sensor with the cross-talk calibrated (REQ-BNIB-009). From the Rev J.1 layout (the C1S nose's DRV5055 pair) until the Rev K layout exists: Noise 5.6 (x) and 6.1 (y) um rms at the tip; the cap's own field 2.8 um, a fixed map to calibrate out; unshielded heel motors 10.2 um at the Rev J.1 place (DEC-045; 15.4 um at Rev J's), turning with the rotor: just over 10 um until it is subtracted by rotor angle; Earth's field 16.8 um, slow; brake and coil fields not computed (CALC)

title: Stray field
requirement: The distance at which the pen's magnetic field falls to the implant limit is measured and stated in the manual; the limit is set from ISO 14117; in Rev K the field comes from B1's magnets and keeper and the heel motors (DEC-050)
rationale: Magnets near implants (Rev J envelope, docs/revJ_plan.md s6); outside the pen the heel motors' rotors dominate the field. Re-scoped for Rev K (DEC-050): B1's four N52 poles and keeper replace the C1S cap. Until the Rev K layout exists, the estimate comes from the Rev J layout
verification: EXP-J07 (the Rev J mock-up now); the same test on Rev K's layout once it exists
current_estimate: From the Rev J layout (the C1S cap) until the Rev K layout exists: 1 mT at about 23 mm from the surface; the magnet cap alone about 10 mm (CALC, free space, motor housings ignored); the 1 mT level is an ASSUMPTION until ISO 14117 and the makers' guidance are read

title: Ink visibility
requirement: With the pen at the writer's own tilt, the fresh ink is visible within 3 mm behind the ball for most writers, for eye positions 40-70 deg above the paper and 0-60 deg to the writer's side of the pen's back direction
rationale: Writers correct their letters by sight; the larger Rev J front hides more at 50 deg than Rev H does. Was: no eye range named (DEC-044 used one assumed eye, 55 deg up and 30 deg to the side)
verification: EXP-J15 (the Rev J.1 window); EXP-J08 (Rev H and Rev J fronts); EXP-J15 repeated on the Rev K front (AC-J15-04, DEC-062)
current_estimate: Rev K (DEC-062, CALC, the same method and eye range): with the 6.0 mm ring and the clear window over the top 240 deg the ink shows within 1 mm in 19 % and within 3 mm in 56 % of cases (median 2.6 mm); with the ring's opening alone 17 % and 50 %. Rev J.1 (DEC-045), the first 15 mm of the sleeve clear over the top 240 deg (hard-coated PC): over tilts 35-75 deg and the eye range, the ink shows within 3 mm in 61 % and within 1 mm in 47 % of cases (Rev J 36 % and 22 %); at 50 deg with the eye 55 deg up and 30 deg to the side, from 3.0 mm (Rev J not within 6 mm) (CALC, eye range ASSUMPTION: no writing-posture source with eye angles could be opened)

title: Page-sensor power
requirement: The page sensor stays on in every mode and draws <= 3 mW from the cell; its stream feeds DEC-042's tremor-line detector
rationale: DEC-042's detector runs on the page sensor, so the steady modes cannot switch it off; a PMW3360-class die takes 34-80 mW, more than the battery per mode allows (REQ-RVJ-I01)
source: DEC-042; DEC-045; OPT-61; AMF-109; docs/revJ1_design.md s4.2
current_estimate: PMW3610-class die, always on: 1.3-1.9 mW (0.60 mA at 1.8 V, MFR OPT-61, x 1.5 for its polling and the regulator, ASSUMPTION; CALC); whether it gives autowrite's 1 kHz, 2 ms and 10 um on paper is unknown (EXP-J10); a PMW3360-class die stays the autowrite fallback

title: Nose command band limit
requirement: The nose command is band-limited to what the nose servo follows: the Rev H tracker's 64 Hz second-order output filter or an equivalent, with its delay inside the prediction horizon
rationale: At lag 0 the listening prediction carried 15-200 Hz content (p99 command speed 0.33 m/s at 10 Hz, 1 mm); the C1S nose missed its command by 890 um rms, and the ink moved 1.6 x as much as with the device off (SIM, tuning writer 100). With the 64 Hz filter, its delay added to the prediction horizon, the same tracker helped. ai2's HW1 nose model did not show this
verification: firmware review and the EXP-L02 bench runs (AC-L02-04); sim2
current_estimate: In sim2 every tracker compared ran with the Rev H tracker's 64 Hz output filter; without it the listening prediction made the ink worse than the device-off pen (SIM, sim2j). DEC-070: the sim2 and sim2j figures here used the legacy ideal sensing (exact velocity, immediate true contact, a 400 Hz loop, page model v1), so they are upper bounds on performance (DEC-070's optimistic bounds), suspended as device evidence until study X reruns them

title: No controller moves tremor-free writing
requirement: Every controller, the heel wheel's modes included, moves tremor-free writing by <= 25 um rms, checked in sim2 against the device-off pen with the same noise
rationale: The project rule on false correction (validation/README.md s2) applied to the whole pen. In sim2 the heel wheel's tremor mode moved tremor-free writing by 0.40 mm (up to 0.50 mm): it steers after the pen with a lag and its tyre resists sideways motion, so fast turns are pulled out of shape. A writer who has learned the wheel was not simulated
source: DEC-047; DEC-048; docs/revJ_simulation.md s6.1, s8.2, s10
verification: sim2 gate on the firmware under test (AC-L02-05); EXP-J18 with people (the wheel's modes)
current_estimate: sim2, test writers 0-4: the guarded tracker G4 0 um; ai2's gated listening tracker 36-85 um (mean 59); the TCN replayed 107-206 um; nose + heel wheel in its tremor mode 324-503 um (mean 403) (SIM): the wheel's tremor mode fails, so DEC-048 keeps the wheel retracted. DEC-070: the sim2 and sim2j figures here used the legacy ideal sensing (exact velocity, immediate true contact, a 400 Hz loop, page model v1), so they are upper bounds on performance (DEC-070's optimistic bounds), suspended as device evidence until study X reruns them

title: Tremor-line detector shut on writing
requirement: The tremor-line detector does not open on the tremor-free writing of the tuning writers of every writer model in use (v1 and v2), with its input restricted to page samples taken while the ball is on the paper
rationale: Tremor-free writing carries spectral lines that a detector can take for tremor: on the intended paths alone ai2's detector reaches peak ratios of 4-6 on v2 writers and 14 on one v1 writer (threshold 5; CALC); sim2's touchdown adds a 9.4 Hz line; with air moves in its input the detector opened on tremor-free writing (SIM, tuning writer 100)
source: DEC-042; DEC-047; docs/revJ_simulation.md s3, s4.1, s10
verification: sim2 gate on the detector build (AC-L01-07); EXP-L01 on real recordings
current_estimate: G4's stricter threshold (open above a peak ratio of 8, close below 4) with ball-on-paper input: no false correction on the tuning writers (v2) or on test writers 0-2 with v1 and v2 (SIM); its rules were fixed before the test (results/sim2j/rules.json). DEC-070: the sim2 and sim2j figures here used the legacy ideal sensing (exact velocity, immediate true contact, a 400 Hz loop, page model v1), so they are upper bounds on performance (DEC-070's optimistic bounds), suspended as device evidence until study X reruns them

title: Filtered nose servo
requirement: The nose servo filters its position signal to its bandwidth, so that the position-sensor noise adds <= 50 mW of coil loss
rationale: sim2's nose servo reads the Hall sensors at 10 kHz with 5.9 um rms of noise and no filter; its derivative action turns the noise into about 0.7 W of coil current (SIM: 2.25 W with the noise and 1.51 W without; with the ball lifted 1.20 W against 0.31 W). A real servo filters its position signal: a firmware requirement, not a hardware change
current_estimate: Unfiltered in sim2: about 0.7 W (SIM, writer 0, tremor-free writing); no filtered servo simulated yet. Study B (SIM): B1's servo acts on a model-based observer of the noisy Hall reading in every sim2 run (REQ-BNIB-009); B1 drew 11.8 mW in tremor-free writing. DEC-070: the sim2 and sim2j figures here used the legacy ideal sensing (exact velocity, immediate true contact, a 400 Hz loop, page model v1), so they are upper bounds on performance (DEC-070's optimistic bounds), suspended as device evidence until study X reruns them

title: Page-sensor drift on paper
requirement: On paper at writing speeds the accumulated (walking) part of the page sensor's position error, fitted from the structure function of its 10 ms window errors, is <= 0.1 mm over 2 s of writing; and its error per 10 ms window, by DeltaPen's own metric (the difference of the translation lengths), is no worse than DeltaPen's (median 24 um, mean 68 um)
rationale: Autowrite, guidance and tracing place the ink by the measured position, so the page error goes straight into the ink: with DeltaPen-like errors that do not add up, autowrite's ink error rose 2-4 x and the text stayed readable; with errors that add up, the letters drifted 1.5-3 mm apart and 7 of 10 words were read (SIM, writers 0-1). The tremor tracker was insensitive. 0.1 mm over 2 s (about one word) is an ASSUMPTION target. DEC-059 judges drift on the part of the error that accumulates: a held error of sim2j's DeltaPen-like size alone gives a raw 2 s difference of 416 um (95th percentile) with nothing accumulating (SIM, docs/measurement_rig.md s3.6). It also compares the window error with DeltaPen's own metric, the error of the translation length (LIT OPT-85), with the vector difference reported beside it. Was (DEC-049): 'On paper at writing speeds the page sensor's position error accumulates by <= 0.1 mm over 2 s of writing, and its error per 10 ms window is no worse than DeltaPen's (median 24 um, mean 68 um)'
source: DEC-049; OPT-02; docs/revJ_simulation.md s6.7, s10; DEC-059; OPT-85; docs/measurement_rig.md s3.6
verification: EXP-J10 (AC-J10-04), measured on rig R10 in EXP-T04
current_estimate: No measurement on paper. DeltaPen (LIT OPT-02, on a tablet surface): 68.3 um mean and 23.6 um median per 10 ms window, 2.6 mm/min drift at rest. sim2 assumes 3 um rms white noise per 1 kHz sample (ASSUMPTION), so its autowrite, tracing and lead-through ink errors are optimistic by up to 2-4 x (SIM). DEC-070: the sim2 and sim2j figures here used the legacy ideal sensing (exact velocity, immediate true contact, a 400 Hz loop, page model v1), so they are upper bounds on performance (DEC-070's optimistic bounds), suspended as device evidence until study X reruns them

title: An added device beats the same pen locked
requirement: A device added to shift the pen (collar, tail module, paper force) enters the product only if it lowers the tremor left at the tip by >= 10 % against the same pen with that device locked and the existing corrector working, at grip 0.5, 1 and 2 x nominal, in the simulator and on the hand phantom, without lowering coverage by more than 5 points
rationale: The review's gate G5 made a requirement for product entry (DEC-051, DEC-053). Relation to the end-cap rules: REQ-EC-002 compares against no module (>= 10 % further reduction on top of the nose) and REQ-EC-003 against the same mass fixed (>= 5 points), both at the measured grip split; this rule is stricter (10 % over the locked device at every grip strength) and adds coverage. It replaces them for product entry: the end-cap is only a bench comparison (DEC-051), and a return to the product is judged here. The phantom part is AC-T16-01 on rig R14 (lower 95 % bound at every grip strength; it was a hypothesis on REQ-EC-003), with the collar of EXP-W11, the tails of EXP-W14 and the end-cap of EXP-K02/J16; REQ-EC-002 and REQ-EC-003 keep their bench lines
source: DEC-051; DEC-053; docs/whole_pen_shift.md (s4.4, s4.5; proposed requirements); independent review 2026-09-29 (G5)
verification: SIM (docs/whole_pen_shift.md s4.4, s4.5); EXP-T16 on rig R14 (AC-T16-01) with EXP-W11, W14, K02 and J16; EXP-W17 (the paper force, AC-W17-01)
current_estimate: SIM (two synthetic test writers, one seed each): the collar with the 87 g Rev J pen inside changed the tremor left by -5 % to +5 % against the same pen with it locked and the nose working (fails); with a light 24 g inner pen 17 % less at 8 mm PD, but 17 points less ink laid (fails on coverage); the 100 g gyroscopic tail 15 / 51 / -14 % at grips 0.5 / 1 / 2 x on the tuning writer and 9 % on test writer 0 (fails). DEC-070: study W's SIM figures ran sim2 with the sim2j firmware on the legacy ideal sensing, so they are upper bounds on performance (DEC-070's optimistic bounds), suspended as device evidence until study X reruns them

title: Collar envelope and travel
requirement: Collar <= 22 mm across; inner barrel <= 12 mm; tip travel >= +/-4 mm at 4-10 Hz under a 1 N writing load; pen <= 55 g in total
rationale: The review's envelope for a whole-pen shifter (a grip of about 22 mm, 40-65 g). Applies to the collar mock-up (EXP-W11 to W13) and to any product collar that later passes REQ-WP-001; DEC-051 puts no whole-pen actuator in the product now. A +/-5 mm collar needs 23.6 mm and +/-6 mm 25.5 mm (CALC)
current_estimate: V2 collar (PROPOSED DESIGN, CALC): 21.7 mm across, 12 mm barrel, flexure pivot 50 mm behind the tip swung +/-4.6 deg for +/-4 mm at the tip (+/-5.2 mm across the page in the tilt plane); 40.1 g in total (collar 18.3 g, inner pen 21.9 g). Not built

title: Writing force through the collar
requirement: The writing force goes through the collar's skid ring and the inner pen carries only its refill spring; static holding power <= 0.2 W at 35 deg and <= 0.06 W at 50 deg
rationale: The review's point 1: the refill spring's side load at the ball costs Rev J's nose 4.72 / 1.63 / 0.17 W at 35 / 50 / 75 deg (REQ-RVJ-N10 asks <= 0.1 W of steady coil heat for the nib). In a V1 collar, where the whole pen swings with its skid ring, the actuators would hold the writing force (0.6-1.2 W, CALC). Applies to the collar mock-up and to any product collar that passes REQ-WP-001
verification: EXP-W11 (current at rest while writing, AC-W11-02)
current_estimate: CALC: 0.16 / 0.055 / 0.006 W at 35 / 50 / 75 deg with the coil plate (F_c cot(theta) z_p on the 42 mm lever)

title: The refill follows the paper through the swing
requirement: The refill follows the paper through the collar's swing while the skid ring is loaded (bounded extension >= z_p x swing x cot(theta_min) + 0.3 mm, about 3.3 mm at 35 deg), and lifts with the pen when the ring unloads, so that strokes do not join
rationale: In the tilt plane the ball must slide along the pen to stay on the paper. SIM: with a +/-0.05 rad, 6 Hz swing the ball stayed on the paper 99.8 % of the time with this stop and 70 % with a stop that follows only the pivot angle (development runs). The collar's counterpart of REQ-RVJ-N09 (Rev J's front stop that follows the nose) and REQ-RVH-008
current_estimate: PROPOSED DESIGN: a load cell on the skid ring tells when it is loaded; in the simulator the stop was bounded to 3 mm beyond the collar-relative stop (wholepen/stepper.py). CALC check (validation pass): the formula gives about 6.0 mm at the full +/-4.6 deg swing and 35 deg (50 mm x 0.080 rad x cot 35 deg + 0.3 mm); 3.3 mm matches about +/-2.4 deg (+/-2.1 mm at the tip): to be settled (validation/README.md s7)

title: The web rests on the collar
requirement: The thumb-index web rests on the collar (a saddle to z >= 97 mm); the swinging barrel clears the web and the sleeve at full swing (fit margin >= 0.3 mm)
rationale: Where the web rests on the moving barrel it takes part of the motion: the ink then moves 0.58-1.23 x the ideal lever, depending on the grip, against 0.78-1.21 x with the web on the collar (CALC, compact 22 g inner pen, grip 0.5-2 x, split 0.3-0.7). Applies to the collar mock-up and to any product collar that passes REQ-WP-001
verification: CAD fit checks (mechanics/cad/wholepen.py); EXP-W11 (the mock-up, AC-W11-05); EXP-W12 (with people, AC-W12-02)
current_estimate: CALC on the CAD: the swung inner pen clears the sleeve by 0.72-1.00 mm and the coil plate by 0.52 mm; saddle to z 97 mm (PROPOSED DESIGN); with the web on the collar the loop keeps a margin >= 0.93 (gain 0.75) over grip 0.5-2 x and split 0.3-0.7

title: Collar loop stable across grips
requirement: With one fixed controller model, the collar's loop stays stable and removes >= 50 % of a 3 mm, 5-9 Hz tremor at grip 0.5-2 x nominal, with the web on the collar
rationale: The review's decisive question for a whole-pen shifter: the grip sets how far the ink moves, and the pen cannot know the grip exactly. CALC: with the compact inner pen and the web on the collar the controller's model is within 6 % in gain and 5 deg in phase and the loop margin is >= 0.93; with the 87 g Rev J pen inside, up to 53 deg. SIM: no causal law was found with which the collar is the main corrector behind a small +/-1 mm nib (its loop became unstable)
current_estimate: CALC: stable at every grip and split with one model. SIM: with perfect knowledge the collar alone removed 64 % of a 3 mm, 6 Hz tremor on the tuning writer (3.31 -> 1.20 mm); as the main corrector behind a +/-1 mm nib with today's estimate the loop was unstable (9-42 % of the ink laid and 4.5 mm left on the tuning writer). DEC-070: study W's SIM figures ran sim2 with the sim2j firmware on the legacy ideal sensing, so they are upper bounds on performance (DEC-070's optimistic bounds), suspended as device evidence until study X reruns them

title: The collar moves only at the tremor line
requirement: The collar moves only at a detected tremor line and only by the share beyond the nib's reach; it never follows letter shapes; tremor-free writing moves <= 25 um with it enabled
rationale: A motion it never makes needs no template and no consent (DEC-051). The 25 um is the programme's false-correction rule (REQ-RVJ-C02 in sim2; validation/README.md s2); the estimate it uses is DEC-052's question
source: DEC-051; DEC-052; docs/whole_pen_shift.md (s3d, s4.3; proposed requirements)
current_estimate: SIM: with the collar enabled tremor-free writing moved at most 8 um; the collar's command is a phasor at the tracked tremor line, gated by the detector, taking only the overflow beyond the nib's reach (at 3 mm with Rev J's nose it stays almost still). DEC-070: study W's SIM figures ran sim2 with the sim2j firmware on the legacy ideal sensing, so they are upper bounds on performance (DEC-070's optimistic bounds), suspended as device evidence until study X reruns them

title: The pivot never reaches its stops
requirement: The collar's pivot never reaches its hard stops in use: the reference stays <= 65 % of the range and a stop-approach limiter backs the servo off
rationale: SIM: with the Rev J pen inside the pivot reached its 0.12 rad stops at 8 mm (peaks 0.16-0.18 rad at ET 8 mm, 0.15 rad at PD 8 mm with perfect knowledge), even with the reference held to 65 % of the range. No limiter was designed or simulated
source: DEC-051; docs/whole_pen_shift.md (s4.3, open issue 4; proposed requirements)
current_estimate: Not met in SIM at 8 mm without a limiter (peaks 0.16-0.18 rad against the 0.12 rad stop). DEC-070: study W's SIM figures ran sim2 with the sim2j firmware on the legacy ideal sensing, so they are upper bounds on performance (DEC-070's optimistic bounds), suspended as device evidence until study X reruns them

title: Felt reaction, noise and unpowered centring
requirement: The reaction the fingers feel stays <= 0.5 N rms of grip-force change; noise <= 35 dBA at 30 cm (ASSUMPTION target); unpowered, a latch centres the inner pen
rationale: The collar pushes back on the sleeve and so on the fingers (the Liftware principle, LIT ACT-16, ACT-17). The flexure is soft (0.02 N m/rad), so without power the inner pen would flop; the latch is not designed (open issue 6)
source: DEC-051; docs/whole_pen_shift.md (s3d, open issue 6; proposed requirements)
current_estimate: SIM grip-force change 0.03-0.38 N rms; noise not estimated; no latch designed. DEC-070: study W's SIM figures ran sim2 with the sim2j firmware on the legacy ideal sensing, so they are upper bounds on performance (DEC-070's optimistic bounds), suspended as device evidence until study X reruns them

title: Tails only against the same mass locked
requirement: A tail module is tested only against the same mass locked (G5) at three grip strengths; a gyroscope stores <= 2 J and excludes a burst by design (stress margin >= 3, over-speed trip)
rationale: DEC-051 rejects inertial tails for the pen: gyroscopic, tuned and reaction-mass tails never robustly beat the same mass locked, and a gyroscope that could matter stores 5-18 J (CALC, SIM). Relation to REQ-EC-007 (the end-cap's CMG research module: <= 3 J, a burst contained, a stop within 2 s): this rule is stricter on energy and asks that a burst be excluded by design, not only contained; it applies to the gyroscope pair of EXP-W14, and REQ-EC-007 keeps its lines for the CMG module (EXP-K06)
source: DEC-051; DEC-053; docs/whole_pen_shift.md (s3b, s3c, s4.5; proposed requirements)
verification: EXP-W14 (AC-W14-01, AC-W14-02); the G5 comparison in EXP-T16 (AC-T16-01)
current_estimate: SIM: the 100 g gyroscopic tail beat its locked mass by 15 / 51 / -14 % at grips 0.5 / 1 / 2 x on the tuning writer and 9 % on test writer 0, and never beat the pen without a tail; tuned and driven masses did no better than the same mass locked. CALC: a gyroscope that could matter stores 5-18 J; the optimum at 100 g 6.4 J. DEC-070: study W's SIM figures ran sim2 with the sim2j firmware on the legacy ideal sensing, so they are upper bounds on performance (DEC-070's optimistic bounds), suspended as device evidence until study X reruns them

title: Gated modes report coverage
requirement: Every gated or ink-only-when-correct mode reports coverage, missing strokes and completion time beside its error
rationale: The ink error falls when ink goes missing (the review). At 8 mm the 'write only when in reach' gate lowered the tremor in the ink laid (ET 2.9 against 3.2 mm) but left 20 of 42 strokes (ET) and 27 (PD) less than half inked, and re-tracing would add 15-18 s to a 15.7 s sentence (SIM). DEC-053. It applies to DEC-049's autowrite of accepted text, which lifts the ball when the text leaves its reach and hands back (REQ-RVJ-N07, REQ-CTRL-014): its coverage is the share of accepted words written in full, its missing strokes the half letters and ink gaps, and its completion time includes the hand-backs (EXP-S19, EXP-N08, EXP-N09); and to the spelling cue's pen lift (DEC-056 (d); EXP-S12, S18)
current_estimate: Study W's results cards report coverage, missing strokes and completion time for every mode (SIM); study S's T9 reports words written in full, half letters per 100 and time against the writer's own (SIM, kinematics only); the earlier autowrite results (nose2, sim2j) report letters and words read and the ink error, not coverage. DEC-070: study W's SIM figures ran sim2 with the sim2j firmware on the legacy ideal sensing, so they are upper bounds on performance (DEC-070's optimistic bounds), suspended as device evidence until study X reruns them

title: Measured-style page sensor by default
requirement: Whole-pen results use the measured-style page sensor (OPT-02 statistics) by default; 3 um white noise only as a labelled bound
rationale: DEC-053. The same rule as REQ-DATA-007 (every tracker simulation reports a measured-error page model, the ideal sensor as a labelled bound; DEC-054), applied to whole-pen devices; sim2's 3 um white noise made autowrite and guidance optimistic by up to 2-4 x (docs/revJ_simulation.md s6.7)
current_estimate: Study W used sim2j's DeltaPen-like walking model (OPT-02 per-window statistics, errors add up) by default (results/wholepen/rules.json). DEC-070: study W's SIM figures ran sim2 with the sim2j firmware on the legacy ideal sensing, so they are upper bounds on performance (DEC-070's optimistic bounds), suspended as device evidence until study X reruns them

title: Static side load left on the nib
requirement: While writing, the static side load left on the nib is <= 10 % of F_s cot(theta) as the mean over 35-75 deg and all rolls, and <= 25 % at the 95th percentile
rationale: The counter-face (DEC-050) balances the paper's push at the refill's rear end, so the coils need not hold F_s cot(theta) (0.21 N at 35 deg with 0.15 N; on the C1S lever 4.7 / 1.6 / 0.17 W at 35 / 50 / 75 deg). DEC-050 is revisited above 25 % (then the clutched bias b' or the unbalanced nib f)
verification: EXP-J17 part (c), the counter-face bench (study B's EXP-B22; AC-J17-04); with Rev K's head mock-up (EXP-K23, DEC-064)
current_estimate: CALC, Monte Carlo over 35-75 deg, all rolls, oil and gel ink, six papers, spring +/-20 % and IMU errors of 1 / 2 deg: residual 5.3 mN mean (6 % of the unbalanced 96 mN), 13.1 mN at the 95th percentile; 16.6 mN pen-up (the moving mass's weight). Rev K's head (DEC-064, CALC Monte Carlo of 20,000 draws, contributors ASSUMPTION): the face off parallel by 1.66 deg on average (3.28 deg at the 95th percentile), leaving 5.7 mN mean and 11.2 mN at the 95th percentile (5.9 % and 13.6 % of F_s cot(theta))

title: Balance released on lift
requirement: When the ball lifts, the pen-up residual is <= 10 % of the contact balance force within 20 ms; at touchdown the full balance returns within 1.0 mm of refill travel at 35 deg (0.6 mm at 75 deg) without a float brake, or within 0.25 mm with one. The float brake is fitted only if EXP-K23 or EXP-J17 (c) shows that the touchdown transient marks the ink
rationale: Nothing may be held in the air: a bias that stays on at a lift pushes the nib over (candidate b without a clutch). The follower stop sets the face 0.25 mm beyond its writing position (a tuned rule). DEC-050 is revisited if the face does not release within 20 ms. DEC-064 (2026-09-30): the counter-face head's face floats +/-0.56 mm to follow the +/-2.5 deg tilt wobble of real writing, so the refill travels up to 0.98 mm at 35 deg (0.58 mm at 75 deg) before the face engages (fit check H6); 0.25 mm would allow only 0.04 mm of wobble. An electro-permanent brake on the float (12-60 mW, ASSUMPTION) would meet 0.25 mm. Was: 'When the ball lifts, the pen-up residual is <= 10 % of the contact balance force within 20 ms; at touchdown the full balance returns within 0.25 mm of refill travel'
source: DEC-050; docs/balanced_nib.md (s1; s4); DEC-064; docs/revK_design.md (s3.4; s11.2)
verification: EXP-J17 part (c) with Rev K's head mock-up (EXP-K23; AC-J17-05); the touchdown transient's ink decides the float brake (AC-K23-05)
current_estimate: Rev K (DEC-064, CALC): float gap 0.56 mm, so 0.98 mm of refill travel at 35 deg and 0.58 mm at 75 deg before the balance returns; the ink tail after a natural lift 0.28-1.1 mm, about 0.3 mm with the brake (ASSUMPTION). Study B: Design rule (CALC); SIM: the face engaged 99.8 % of the contact time and 6.7 % of the pen-up time (face gap 0.25 mm, a frozen rule). DEC-070: study B's sim2 figures used the legacy ideal sensing, so they are upper bounds on performance (DEC-070's optimistic bounds), suspended as device evidence until study X reruns them

title: Usable travel under load
requirement: Usable nib travel >= +/-1.0 mm at 35 deg and 12 Hz with the coil 90 K above ambient, a 3.3 V supply and Km at 0.7 x the image-method value
rationale: DEC-050: +/-1.0 mm for the one-axis demonstrator (G3); the two-axis nib (G4) at +/-1.5 mm only if study E finds a causal estimator that uses the extra reach on real severe tremor, else +/-1.0 mm. Study R's severe class is typically 1.7 mm peak at the tip, so +/-1 mm covers the mild and moderate classes and part of the severe one; tremor beyond the reach stays uncorrected (DEC-051). The image-method Km is an upper bound, so the travel is sized at 0.7 x. For the product it replaces REQ-RVJ-N01's 6.0 mm (the C1S nose, DEC-050). DEC-060 (study E, 2026-09-30): no causal estimator uses reach beyond +/-1 mm on real tremor, so the G4 nib is +/-1.0 mm too. Study F (2026-09-30; SIM, the Rev J nose with its travel cut, tuning split): with +/-1.0 mm even perfect knowledge gains only 1.4 words at the severe class, below DEC-055's +2, so Rev K's nib makes no severe-tremor legibility claim (DEC-060); EXP-E23 checks B1's own reach in sim2. Study N (DEC-083): the reach candidate's travel is REQ-BNIB-018 (+/-1.5 mm); this +/-1.0 mm stays for the margin candidate until DEC-096 chooses (DEC-072)
verification: EXP-T10 (study B's EXP-B26; AC-T10-05); the Km map in EXP-T07 (study B's EXP-B23; AC-T07-01); EXP-E23 (AC-E23-01: the reach against DEC-055's words line at the severe class, in sim2)
current_estimate: CALC: +/-1.06 mm under the 35 deg load with Km x 0.7, a hot coil and 3.3 V; the same architecture at +/-1.5 mm draws 23.2 / 34.3 mW (Km x 0.85 / 0.7) with 2.91 g moving. SIM (ET 8 Hz 1 mm, writer 0): the handle's tremor passes +/-1.06 mm 10 % of the time; the +/-1.5 mm variant leaves 57 % less. Rev K (DEC-062, CALC; tolerances ASSUMPTION): the stops sit up to 0.072 mm off the magnetic centre at the 99th percentile, so the usable travel in the worst direction falls to 0.99 mm at the 1st percentile (0.98 mm at worst), just under +/-1.0 mm. Study F (SIM, s8): perfect knowledge leaves 1.00 mm at the severe class with +/-1.0 mm, a gain of 1.4 (0.8 to 1.9) words read, and 0.67 mm with +/-1.5 mm, 3.2 (2.6 to 3.7) words; the command that cancels severe tremor exceeds 1.0 mm 61 % of the time; an estimate that itself leaves the +2 residual keeps it only with about +/-2-3 mm. DEC-070: study B's sim2 figures used the legacy ideal sensing, so they are upper bounds on performance (DEC-070's optimistic bounds), suspended as device evidence until study X reruns them

title: Continuous nib power
requirement: Continuous nib power at duty A (0.2 mm rms, 8 Hz, 70 % contact) <= 20 mW as the mean over 35-75 deg; holding coil heat <= 0.1 W at every tilt and roll (REQ-RVJ-N10)
rationale: The balance leaves mostly the ball's drag, which grows with the ink force: about 8 / 30 / 184 mW at 0.15 / 0.3 / 0.69 N (CALC), so gate G1's force sets the power (DEC-050). The holding part is REQ-RVJ-N10 (AC-J17-02); this requirement adds the continuous power. Study N (DEC-080): restated with the convention in REQ-BNIB-019 (<= 45 mW at the weakest point x 0.7; <= 20 mW at the centre x 1.0); Rev K's B1 (matched) 64.6 / 19.9 mW (CALC)
verification: EXP-T13 (study B's EXP-B27; AC-T13-04); EXP-J17 (AC-J17-02, the holding part); EXP-T15 (study B's EXP-B29)
