current_estimate: CALC: 7.6 mW at duty A with the image-method Km (10.5 mW at 0.85 x, 15.4 mW at 0.7 x; 17.6 mW at 35 deg); holding at most 1.6 mW (3.2 mW at 0.7 x). SIM (sim2, 4 synthetic writers): 14.8 mW while correcting and 11.8 mW in tremor-free writing; the same nib unbalanced 70 mW. DEC-070: study B's sim2 figures used the legacy ideal sensing, so they are upper bounds on performance (DEC-070's optimistic bounds), suspended as device evidence until study X reruns them

title: Tip-equivalent moving mass
requirement: Tip-equivalent moving mass of the nib <= 4.5 g
rationale: A light moving part needs little force to follow tremor and keeps the power low; the C1S nose and a long-arm gimbal carry 5-15 g at the tip (DEC-050). Study N: tightened to 3.5 g in REQ-BNIB-021
current_estimate: CALC 3.49 g (B1 at the +/-1.0 mm travel floor)

title: First parasitic mode and bandwidth
requirement: The nib's lowest structural mode, with the ball free and with the ball stuck on the paper, is >= 2.5 x the servo's closed-loop bandwidth; closed-loop bandwidth >= 40 Hz
rationale: The first parasitic mode sets the usable servo bandwidth (about the mode / 3). For the product nib this replaces REQ-RVJ-N02's C1S lines (bandwidth >= 60 Hz, first mode >= 240 Hz), which stay for the C1S bench research module (DEC-050). DEC-050 (the lead, 2026-09-30) sets the rule with the ball stuck: at least 2.5 x the servo bandwidth with the ball free (362 Hz) and stuck (109 Hz, the suspension on the stuck ball), so with the ball stuck the bandwidth may not exceed about 44 Hz (CALC). Was: 'First parasitic mode of the loaded nib, with the ball free and with the ball stuck on the paper, >= 120 Hz; closed-loop bandwidth >= 40 Hz'. DEC-066 (2026-09-30): Rev K's position servo runs at 40 Hz and its inner loop at <= 46 Hz, inside the rule; DEC-066 is revisited if EXP-T10 measures a stuck mode below 100 Hz (AC-T10-08)
verification: EXP-T10 (study B's EXP-B26; AC-T10-02); AC-T10-08 (DEC-066's 100 Hz)
current_estimate: CALC, loaded eigenmodes of the refill and carrier: ball free 6 (the suspension on the wires), 362, 2445 Hz; ball stuck 109 (the suspension on the stuck ball), 568, 2509 Hz; study B counts 362 Hz as the first parasitic mode; at 40 Hz of bandwidth the rule of DEC-050 gives 9.1 x (ball free) and 2.7 x (ball stuck). Rev K (DEC-066, study K CALC): with the C17200 wires and the ball thrust guide the ball-free mode is 1206 Hz and the ball-stuck mode 163 Hz nominal and 115 Hz worst (35 deg, soft refill, 20 um of pre-sliding), so the servo may run at up to 46 Hz (65 Hz nominally); 46 Hz is 1.15 x the 40 Hz floor (marginal)

title: Suspension fatigue
requirement: The wire suspension has a Goodman safety factor >= 1.5 at the stop travel for 43.2 M cycles, with the clamp's stress concentration included
rationale: Four 0.128 mm Ti-6Al-4V wires carry the carrier; 43.2 M cycles at the stop travel is the design life. Fatigue with real clamps is unproven (Kt 1.3-2.5 ASSUMED). DEC-050 is revisited if the wire coupons fail before 43.2 M cycles. In Rev K the four wires are 0.10 mm C17200 and carry the coil currents (DEC-063; REQ-RVK-004)
verification: EXP-B25 (AC-B25-01, study B's Ti wires); Rev K's C17200 wires (DEC-063): EXP-K21 (AC-K21-04, with AC-K21-02 and AC-K21-03)
current_estimate: CALC: full-stop strain 0.68e-3 and stress 139 MPa with Kt 1.8, Goodman safety factor 3.25 at 43.2 M cycles (Ti-6Al-4V 530 MPa x 0.85, AMF-20 low end, ASSUMPTION); tolerance Monte Carlo 1.62 / 1.77 / 2.49 at the 1st / 5th / 50th percentile. Rev K's C17200 wires (DEC-063, CALC; fatigue strength MFR AMF-19 x 0.85): Goodman safety factor 2.18 at Kt 1.8 and 1.57 at Kt 2.5; at the 5th percentile 1.40 with <= 0.05 N of assembly preload (marginal) and 0.92 with up to 0.3 N

title: Ink force at the ball
requirement: The ink force at the ball is the set value +/-20 % over 35-75 deg with the balance engaged
rationale: With the counter-face the paper-normal force equals the spring's push on the face; the set value itself is frozen only after gate G1 measures the minimum reliable ink force (DEC-050, REQ-BNIB-014). For the product it replaces REQ-RVJ-N05's 0.15 N +/-20 % (the C1S drum spring)
verification: EXP-J17 part (c) (AC-J17-07); EXP-T02 for the set value (study B's EXP-B20)
current_estimate: CALC: the paper-normal force equals the face's push with the face engaged; the set value is not frozen (0.15 N in study B's models, ASSUMPTION)

title: Nib position sensing and a filtered servo
requirement: Nib position sensing <= 2 um rms tip-referred at 1 kHz with the coils driven (cross-talk calibrated); the servo acts on an observer's estimate, never on the raw Hall reading
rationale: An unfiltered servo reacting to Hall noise cost the C1S nose about 0.7 W in sim2 (REQ-RVJ-C04, DEC-046). This is its B1 form: a TMAG5170-class 3-D Hall sensor and a 1 mm N52 cube
current_estimate: CALC 0.99 um; SIM: the filtered servo (a model-based observer on the noisy Hall reading) in every sim2 run. DEC-070: study B's sim2 figures used the legacy ideal sensing, so they are upper bounds on performance (DEC-070's optimistic bounds), suspended as device evidence until study X reruns them

title: Skin temperature
requirement: Skin temperature <= 41 degC in a 30 degC room at 35 deg with 2 mm tremor for 30 min, with the governor in the loop
rationale: The design target of REQ-THM-001 (43 degC absolute in a rated 30 degC room, 41 degC as the target) at B1's largest load. For the product it replaces REQ-RVJ-N03's autowrite heat rule (the C1S nose, now a bench research module). Study N: REQ-BNIB-022 names the severe-tremor duty; under it Rev K's B1 reaches 37.8 degC and the balanced candidate 33.7 degC (CALC)
current_estimate: SIM + CALC: 24.4 mW at 35 deg with 2 mm ET tremor; after 30 min coil 31.2 degC and skin 30.8 degC, the governor never acting; the same nib unbalanced 38.3 / 35.7 degC. DEC-070: study B's sim2 figures used the legacy ideal sensing, so they are upper bounds on performance (DEC-070's optimistic bounds), suspended as device evidence until study X reruns them

title: Unpowered state
requirement: Unpowered, the nib rests on its soft stop (<= 1.3 mm off centre) and the pen writes like a normal pen
rationale: A failure or a flat battery must leave an ordinary pen; the face still balances without power. DEC-062 (2026-09-30): no wire suspension soft enough for B1's power can hold the 3.4 g moving nib against gravity: the wires alone would let it sag 18 mm, and study B's 3.8 N/m 7 mm (fit check N22), so the unpowered nib rests on its soft stop. Was: 'Unpowered, the nib is centred by its suspension within 0.1 mm and the pen writes like a normal pen'
current_estimate: Rev K (DEC-062, CALC): gravity rests the unpowered nib on its soft stop, 1.26 mm off centre, and the pen still writes; the stops sit up to 0.072 mm off the magnetic centre at the 99th percentile (tolerances ASSUMPTION). Was (study B): 'CALC (the failure state): centred by the wires (3.8 N/m at the tip), the face still balancing'; under gravity those wires would let the nib sag 7 mm

title: Drop
requirement: After a 1 m drop onto a hard floor the wires stay elastic (axial stops <= 20 um) and the face and its positioners are undamaged
rationale: The four wires buckle sideways at 0.08 N of compression in all; axial stops carry a drop
current_estimate: CALC (flexure.shock): at 100 g the wires take 66 MPa without the stop; at 500 and 2000 g the stops engage and the wires take 85 MPa; buckled wires stay elastic behind 20 um stops

title: The nib's interface file
requirement: The nib's physical interface lives in config/nib.yaml (versioned); the simulators and the other studies read it
rationale: One versioned definition (forces, the friction map, Km over the stroke, moving mass and suspension, travel, sensors, thermal parameters, the counter-face, the drive, the failure state and the C1S reference values), each leaf with a unit and an evidence status, so that measured values replace calculated ones in one place. Study N: REQ-BNIB-025 adds the matched model's inputs (DEC-080)
verification: bnib tests (the file against the code); review at the gates (AC-T13-06)
current_estimate: config/nib.yaml is generated by python3 -m bnib.run_study and checked against the code by bnib/tests (study B)

title: Minimum ink force known before the spring is frozen
requirement: The minimum reliable ink force is known per tip type and paper (six papers), over 35-75 deg and 5-60 mm/s, before the refill spring force is frozen
rationale: No source gives a minimum: the design's 0.15 N is 4.6 x below the lowest maker's test load found (0.69 N at 70 deg, LIT CON-97). The balance works at any force, but B1's power grows with it through the ball's drag, so the spring force is frozen only after G1 (DEC-050). DEC-050 is revisited above about 0.3 N
current_estimate: Not known: no source states a minimum for any tip type; the test loads found are 0.69-1.5 N (LIT CON-97, CON-96, CON-23, CON-21)

title: Face orientation sensing
requirement: While writing, the IMU's tilt error is <= 1 deg and its roll error <= 2 deg (1 sigma) for the face schedule
rationale: The face is set parallel to the paper from the IMU's tilt and roll by three small screw motors with no holding power. The IMU sees gravity, not the page, so a sloped desk leaves F_n sin(slope) across the pen (about 17 / 34 / 67 mN at 5 / 10 / 20 deg: 2 / 7 / 28 mW of holding); a slope setting in the app or the slide cam (c') removes it
verification: EXP-B28 (AC-B28-01, AC-B28-02); EXP-B30 (the keyed grip, AC-B30-01)
current_estimate: ASSUMPTION (1 and 2 deg in the balance Monte Carlo); the face schedule lags the pen's tilt wobble (about +/-2.5 deg, LIT CON-02) by about 2 deg at 1 Hz with a 0.2 s response (CALC)

title: Refill guide friction
requirement: The refill guide's friction coefficient is <= 0.01 (a ball or roller guide)
rationale: The counter-face turns the static load into a couple that loads the two refill bushings with 1.0 / 0.6 / 0.19 N in all at 35 / 50 / 75 deg (CALC); the slide friction then acts across the pen as h cot(theta). PTFE sleeves (0.05) double B1's power; bare metal (0.1) breaks REQ-RVJ-N10 at 35 deg
current_estimate: ASSUMPTION mu_g 0.005 (a rolling guide): h 5.1 mN and B1 at 7.3 mW; PTFE (0.05): 16.2 mW and up to 33 mW of holding while the refill sticks; bare metal (0.1): 43 mW and 133 mW stuck (CALC)

title: Page sensor lift range
requirement: The page sensor keeps the page through the lifts between strokes: lift cut-off >= 2 mm above the writing height (OPT-54 class)
rationale: SIM: with a 0.8 mm cut-off the firmware lost the page at every lift and faded its authority back in at the start of every stroke; B1's tracker then left 0.87 of the tremor instead of 0.83, and perfect knowledge 0.40 instead of 0.28. It goes with the page sensor's own requirements (REQ-RVJ-N06, REQ-RVJ-C05). DEC-062 (2026-09-30) keeps it as the page sensor's selection requirement: the PMW3610-class die of Rev K's layout tracks the page only within +/-0.2 mm of its lens height (MFR OPT-61; fit check F5 fails), so EXP-T04 (AC-T04-07) chooses the die and optics
source: DEC-050; docs/balanced_nib.md (s4; s5.3); MFR OPT-54; DEC-062; OPT-61
current_estimate: Rev K (DEC-062): a PMW3610-class die tracks within +/-0.2 mm of its lens height (MFR OPT-61), against the 2 mm asked (fit check F5, CALC). Study B: SIM: the H1 writer lifts the handle 1.20 mm (median; 1.44 mm at the 90th percentile) between strokes; with the sensor's 2.0 mm cut-off the page is kept through every lift. DEC-070: study B's sim2 figures used the legacy ideal sensing, so they are upper bounds on performance (DEC-070's optimistic bounds), suspended as device evidence until study X reruns them

title: Usable travel of the reach candidate
requirement: For the reach candidate (study N's balanced nib; DEC-083): usable nib travel >= +/-1.5 mm at 35 deg and 12 Hz with the coil hot, a 3.3 V supply and K_m at 0.7 x the weakest point. REQ-BNIB-003's +/-1.0 mm stays for the margin candidate until DEC-096 chooses between them (DEC-072)
rationale: Study N proposed it as an edit of REQ-BNIB-003 (+/-1.5 mm, was +/-1.0 mm). Study F: +/-1.5 mm is the least reach that gives +2 words at the severe class with perfect knowledge; with the +2-words estimator the balanced nib leaves 0.82 mm, so the reach meets DEC-067's target only with a better estimator (study N s4.3). DEC-072 as refined by study N: the reach candidate is the balanced design, and the choice against the margin candidate waits for measured loads (DEC-096)
source: DEC-083; DEC-072; DEC-096; docs/nib_optimisation.md (s4.3; s5; s9.2)
current_estimate: CALC (study N): +/-1.50 mm at 2.48 V, the stop at 1.70 mm

title: Continuous nib power, convention stated
requirement: Continuous nib power at duty A (0.2 mm rms, 8 Hz, 70 % contact) <= 45 mW as the mean over 35-75 deg at the weakest point x 0.7 (<= 20 mW at the centre x 1.0)
rationale: Study N proposed it as an edit of REQ-BNIB-004, whose 20 mW read in effect as the centre x 1.0; DEC-080 states the convention. Under it Rev K's B1 (matched) takes 64.6 mW, so the margin candidate meets only the centre line (19.9 mW)
verification: EXP-T13 (AC-T13-07); EXP-NB09 (the rig's loss against the model)
current_estimate: CALC (study N): the balanced candidate 37.9 mW at the weakest point x 0.7 and 8.3 mW at the centre x 1.0; Rev K's B1 (matched) 64.6 / 19.9 mW

title: Worst-case screen
requirement: The worst-case screen (full radius, 4-12 Hz, eight directions, matched loads, the weakest point x 0.7, the coil hot) takes <= 0.15 W
rationale: The pass's allocation (DEC-072, DEC-096), judged with study N's matched loads: the pass's 1.5 mm nib takes 0.43 W and warms the skin to 46.3 degC (study N)
current_estimate: CALC (study N): the balanced candidate 0.107 W; Rev K's B1 (matched) 0.17 W; the pass's 1.5 mm nib 0.43 W

title: Tip-equivalent moving mass, tightened
requirement: Tip-equivalent moving mass of the nib <= 3.5 g
rationale: Study N proposed it as an edit of REQ-BNIB-005 (was 4.5 g): +1 g of moving mass adds about 20 % to the typical loss (CALC)
current_estimate: CALC (study N): the balanced candidate 3.29 g (coils 1.15 g, titanium flange 0.73 g, refill 0.84 g, holder extension 0.30 g); Rev K's B1 3.44 g

title: Skin temperature under the severe-tremor duty
requirement: Skin <= 41 degC in a 30 degC room at 35 deg under the severe-tremor correction duty (study F's +2-words command, clipped at the reach) for 30 min, with the governor in the loop
rationale: Study N proposed it as an edit of REQ-BNIB-010 that names the duty (REQ-BNIB-010 used 2 mm of tremor); the pass's 1.5 mm nib reaches 46.3 degC under this duty (study N). The limit is REQ-THM-001's design target
current_estimate: CALC (study N, study K's fin model): the balanced candidate 33.7 degC; Rev K's B1 37.8 degC; the pass's 1.5 mm nib 46.3 degC

title: Weight in contact in the budgets
requirement: The nib budgets hold the moving mass's weight in contact unless EXP-NB06 shows a weight trim that keeps REQ-BNIB-001
rationale: Study K's sums set the weight aside while the ball is on the paper; a face scheduled to cancel it would cut the balanced candidate's typical loss by 16 %, but it is not proven (study N)
current_estimate: CALC (study N): the weight is 11.5 of the balanced candidate's 37.9 mW; the trim -16 %, not assumed

title: Lead heating and clearance
requirement: Lead heating <= 45 K above the clamps at the severe duty's rms current, and the leads >= 0.3 mm clear of the rear race at the stop
rationale: The pass's screen limits the leads' heating to 45 K; the leads pass inside the full-ring rear race (study N)
verification: EXP-NB04 (AC-NB04-04, the heating); EXP-NB08 (AC-NB08-03, the clearance on the built nib)
current_estimate: CALC (study N): the balanced candidate 1.1 K, with 0.08 mm of margin on the lead circle; study K's B1 -0.04 mm

title: The nib's interface file carries the matched model
requirement: config/nib.yaml also carries the matched model's inputs: the moving mass, the force map (measured once EXP-NB01 reports), the anchor's stiffness, the guide's preload and the leads' resistance
rationale: Study N proposed it as an edit of REQ-BNIB-013: the simulators and the budgets read one set (DEC-080)
current_estimate: Study N's inputs are listed with their labels in results/nibopt/nibopt.json; config/nib.yaml does not carry them yet

title: Rev K envelope
requirement: Rev K (DEC-062): <= 24 mm across where held, <= 150 mm long, and <= 75 g with every module fitted (the heel module included)
rationale: Study K's layout is 145.1 mm long and 24 mm where held from 20 mm behind the tip; it weighs 66.4 g, and 73.4 g with the heel module (CALC). The limits leave room for the build (docs/revK_design.md s11.2). The 24 mm grip is DEC-029's; Rev H's envelope allowed <= 175 mm and <= 110 g (REQ-RVH-001). In study E's simulation the heavier Rev J pen added tip tremor (1.08-1.09 x a 12 g pen's, SIM), which EXP-W01 tests with people. Study N (DEC-083, 2026-09-30): the balanced +/-1.5 mm nib needs 157.1 mm (REQ-RVK-007); the lead keeps 150 mm until writers try a 157 mm dummy (EXP-J09, EXP-K24), and k_envelope (+/-1.47 mm) fits in 149.7 mm
verification: EXP-M03 (AC-M03-08, the built pens); EXP-J09 (AC-J09-02, a 66 g dummy with writers); CALC; EXP-J09 with a 157 mm dummy (AC-J09-03, DEC-083)
current_estimate: CALC (study K, with +10 % for wiring and adhesive as Rev J): the base pen 145.1 mm and 66.4 g, balance point 74.9 mm from the tip; with the heel module 73.4 g and 77.4 mm; 24 mm where held from z 20 mm, the front 12 mm across at the skid ring and widening to 24 mm over 14 mm. Rev J.1 was 84.3 g; study B estimated 68.8 g

title: Rev K battery per mode
requirement: Battery, continuous writing on the LIR14500 at 23 C (Rev K, DEC-062): >= 16 h in every writing mode up to 2 mm of tremor, the spelling cue included; >= 8 h of lead-through with the heel module; the page sensor stays on in every mode
rationale: For Rev K it replaces REQ-RVJ-I01's rows (docs/revK_design.md s11.2). Study K's low ends assume magnets 30 % weaker than modelled and the electronics at the top of their datasheet range: 21.0 h at 2 mm of tremor and 10.8 h in lead-through (CALC). The page sensor feeds the tremor-line detector, so it stays on (REQ-RVJ-I07). Autowrite is not a Rev K mode (DEC-050); its rows stay in REQ-RVJ-I01 for the C1S bench research module
source: DEC-062; DEC-065; docs/revK_design.md (s5.2; s11.2); AMF-80; OPT-61
verification: EXP-P01 (per-mode runtime on the built pen, AC-P01-06); EXP-J12 (electronics); CALC
current_estimate: CALC (study K, 2.22 Wh usable): steady writing 24.2-50.1 h with no tremor, 23.5-48.6 h at 1 mm and 21.0-48.4 h at 2 mm (the nib clips); guide 23.2-48.9 h; spelling cue with lifts and ticks 23.7-50.0 h; with the heel module, lead-through 10.8-15.0 h and guide with the heel steering 18.2-39.4 h. The electronics take about half the power (21.9-43.1 mW) and the nib the other half (17.8-36.3 mW at 1 mm), mostly to hold the 3.4 g moving mass against gravity. Study N (DEC-080, the matched model at the weakest point x 0.7, the electronics at their high end): Rev K's B1 17.6-18.6 h at the cautious end in every mode, the balanced candidate 22.3-23.3 h; REQ-RVK-009 states the convention

title: Suspension carries the counter-face couple
requirement: The nib's suspension carries the counter-face couple (>= 11 mN m at 35 deg) with no wire in compression beyond 0.5 x its buckling load, and the carrier tilts by no more than 0.2 mrad
rationale: The paper's push on the ball and the face's push on the refill's rear end are parallel but 67.8 mm apart: a couple of 10.9 mN m at 35 deg (8.5 at 50 deg, 3.4 at 75 deg). On the wires alone it puts 0.70 N of compression on a wire, 81 x the buckling load of a 0.10 mm C17200 wire (0.009 N; fit check N14, study B's B1 as drawn), and with the compressed pair buckled the ball-stuck mode drops to 86 Hz (CALC). DEC-063 adds a sprung ball thrust guide on the carrier's flange, so the wires only centre the carrier and carry the current
verification: EXP-K20 (AC-K20-02, the ball thrust guide coupon)
current_estimate: CALC (study K): with the ball guide (2 x 6 Si3N4 balls of 0.8 mm on a 16.6 mm circle, lapped 440C races on wave springs preloaded to 4 N, about 1.5 x the couple's ball load) the loaded balls carry 2.6 N at 35 deg, the rolling friction is 2.6 mN (rolling resistance 0.001, ASSUMPTION), no wire is in compression and the carrier's tilt and axial position are fixed; Hertz stress 2.66 GPa at the couple's load and 3.05 GPa at the springs' release load; ball-free mode 1206 Hz. Study N (DEC-082): the 4 N preload gives about 8.1 mN of drag and 2.7 GPa; the preload is set from the couple instead (REQ-RVK-010, REQ-RVK-011): the balanced candidate 1.82 N per race, 3.95 mN, 2.16 GPa

title: Leads to the moving coils
requirement: Each lead to the moving coils has <= 0.3 ohm, and no lead fails by fatigue in 43.2 M cycles at the stop travel while carrying 0.1 A
rationale: The two moving coils need four leads across the moving carrier. Study B's Ti-6Al-4V wires have 3.5 ohm each (170 uOhm cm, AMF-21 re-read), which triples the coil loop and caps the current at 0.34 A at 3.3 V (fit check N17). DEC-063 makes the four suspension wires the leads, in 0.10 mm C17200 beryllium copper, the way optical-disc pickups feed their coils (practice). 43.2 M cycles at the stop travel is the design life of REQ-BNIB-007
source: DEC-063; docs/revK_design.md (s3.3; s11.2); AMF-18; AMF-19; AMF-251
current_estimate: CALC (study K): 0.27 ohm per 0.10 mm C17200 wire at 22 % IACS minimum (MFR AMF-251; AMF-18 gives 22-28 %); the coil loop rises from 2.5 to 3.03 ohm (+21 % copper loss) and the current limit at 3.3 V is 1.0 A. Fatigue at the stop: Goodman safety factor 2.18 (Kt 1.8) and 1.57 (Kt 2.5); 1.40 at the 5th percentile with <= 0.05 N of assembly preload and 0.92 with up to 0.3 N (REQ-BNIB-007 asks 1.5); a 0.08 mm wire reaches 1.50 at +33 % loop loss. Not tested with current. Study N (DEC-082): with study K's stiff anchor (0.01 N/um) the stretched leads carry 0.31 N at the stop and the Goodman factor is 0.71; the floating anchor (REQ-RVK-008) with eight leads in parallel pairs gives 1.53 at the worst corner for the balanced candidate (CALC)

title: Coil clearance at the stop
requirement: The moving coils stay >= 0.2 mm off the bore at the stop after the centring tolerances (99th percentile), and >= 0 mm in a 1 m sideways drop
rationale: Rev K's coils are wound coils sized to stay 0.3 mm inside the bore at the stop; study B's idealised coil reached 10.81 mm from the axis at the stop against a 10.7 mm limit (fit check N3), and a coil that can be wound, with the same legs, would reach 12.9 mm. The centring tolerances eat the clearance, and in a drop the stop yields (docs/revK_design.md s3.3, s3.5)
verification: EXP-B25 (AC-B25-04: the first build's offsets on its jig, and 1 m sideways drops)
current_estimate: CALC (study K; tolerances ASSUMPTION): the stops sit up to 0.072 mm off the magnetic centre at the 99th percentile, and the 0.3 mm running clearances fall to 0.21-0.26 mm (the coil against the bore 0.21 mm). In a 1 m sideways drop the titanium stop bush (1e6 N/m, ASSUMPTION) yields 0.26 mm and the coils stay 0.04 mm off the bore (fit check N21, marginal); a TPE or PEEK stop would yield 0.8-1.8 mm and let them strike it

title: Nib figures state the force-constant convention
requirement: Every nib power, skin or battery figure states its force-constant convention and is computed with the matched model (DEC-080): gravity on the moving mass held in contact unless a weight trim is proven, study K's face-residual Monte Carlo, the ball's writing drag at N = F_n, the guide's drag from its preload, nonlinear wires at the design's anchor, coil and magnet at the fin model's temperature; the headline uses the weakest singular value over the usable disk x 0.7, with the centre x 1.0 stated beside it until EXP-NB01 measures the map
rationale: Study K's 16.6 mW and the pass's 0.081 W differ mostly by convention: the weakest point x 0.7 multiplies the stated power by about 3.25 against study K's centre value, while physics adds only 17 -> 20 mW (docs/nib_optimisation.md s2.5). DEC-080 (the lead): every nib force and power claim uses the weakest-point force constant x 0.7
verification: review of every nib claim and prediction (AC-NB01-05); EXP-NB01 (the measured map replaces the derating)
current_estimate: CALC (study N, matched model): Rev K's B1 about 65 mW typical at the weakest point x 0.7 (20 mW at the centre x 1.0); the balanced candidate 37.9 mW (8.3 mW); the pass's 1.5 mm nib 0.43 W in the worst-case screen, not 0.081 W

title: Envelope with the +/-1.5 mm nib
requirement: With the balanced +/-1.5 mm nib (DEC-083): <= 24 mm across where held, <= 158 mm long and <= 75 g with every module fitted (<= 150 mm with a +/-1.47 mm nib). It takes effect only once writers accept a 157 mm dummy (EXP-J09, EXP-K24; the lead's note on DEC-083); until then REQ-RVK-001's 150 mm stands
rationale: Study N: the second magnet array adds 7.0 mm of stack and the 32 mm leads 5.3 mm, so the balanced candidate is 157.1 mm long; inside 150 mm the best found is +/-1.47 mm (k_envelope, 149.7 mm, 56.0 mW typical). Study N proposed it as an edit of REQ-RVK-001 ('<= 24 mm across where held, <= 158 mm long with the +/-1.5 mm nib (<= 150 mm with a +/-1.47 mm nib), <= 75 g with every module'); the lead keeps 150 mm until the dummy trial (DEC-083)
verification: EXP-J09 (AC-J09-03, writers with a 157 mm dummy); EXP-M03 (AC-M03-09, the built pen)
current_estimate: CALC (study N): the balanced candidate 24.0 mm, 157.1 mm and 70.4 g, balance point 81.4 mm from the tip; k_envelope 23.5 mm, 149.7 mm and 65.9 g

title: Floating anchor for the leads
requirement: The leads' anchor is designed at an axial stiffness of 50-500 N/m including the flex lead (the range study N searched); the built anchor is within +/-20 % of its design value; with the built value the leads carry <= 15 mN of tension at the stop
rationale: Bent wires gain tension against a stiff anchor: study K's 10,000 N/m (0.01 N/um) gives 0.31 N at the stop and a Goodman factor of 0.71, where REQ-BNIB-007 asks 1.5; DEC-082 withdraws it and floats the anchor (study N)
current_estimate: CALC (study N): the balanced candidate 50 N/m (27 N/m of 25 um etched 301 leaves and the pass's 23.4 N/m allowance for the flex lead, ASSUMPTION) and 7.7 mN at the stop; study K's anchor 0.31 N (Goodman 0.71)

title: Battery per mode, convention stated
requirement: Battery, continuous writing on the LIR14500: >= 16 h in every writing mode up to 2 mm of tremor, with the nib's loss at the weakest point x 0.7 and the electronics at their high end (REQ-RVK-002 with DEC-080's convention)
rationale: Study N proposed it as an edit of REQ-RVK-002: the same 16 h, with the convention stated (DEC-080). Every study N candidate keeps 16 h in every mode at the cautious end (17.6 h is the lowest, Rev K's B1 guiding)
verification: EXP-P01 (AC-P01-07, the prediction before the build; AC-P01-06 on the built pen)
current_estimate: CALC (study N, 2.22 Wh, conservative - optimistic): the balanced candidate 22.3-23.3 h at the cautious end in every mode (60.1-61.6 h optimistic); Rev K's B1 (matched) 17.6-18.6 h (45.7-47.5 h)

title: Guide preload set from the couple
requirement: Ball-guide preload per race >= 1.2 x the preload at which a ball first unloads under the 35 deg couple, and <= 2 N; the guide's drag <= 5 mN at 35 deg
rationale: DEC-082 withdraws study K's 4 N preload: it gives about 8.1 mN of drag, above EXP-K20's 5 mN line, and 2.7 GPa of contact stress. The drag is the rolling coefficient x the total ball load, which the preload sets (study N)
current_estimate: CALC (study N): the balanced candidate 1.82 N per race (floor 1.31 N) and 3.95 mN of drag (rolling coefficient 0.001, ASSUMPTION; THK's catalogue shows friction rising at light load, AMF-262)

title: Guide contact stress
requirement: Peak Hertz stress in the ball guide <= 3.33 GPa under the sustained writing load and <= 3.67 GPa at the race springs' release in a drop
rationale: A ball's basic static load rating is the load that gives 4,200 MPa at the most heavily loaded contact, about 0.0001 of the ball diameter of permanent set (AMF-260); static safety factors of 2 for quiet, accurate running and 1.5 for shock (AMF-261) give 3.33 and 3.67 GPa, the stress scaling with the cube root of the load (rotating-bearing practice applied to a sphere on a flat, ASSUMPTION)
current_estimate: CALC (study N): the balanced candidate 2.16 GPa sustained and 2.17 GPa at a drop; study K's guide at 4 N about 2.7 GPa

title: Drive voltage headroom
requirement: The worst-case screen's peak force, with the coil hot and back-EMF included, needs <= 3.3 V at the driver
rationale: The 3.3 V bus is the low-battery supply (ASSUMPTION, study B); the pass's 1.5 mm nib needs 3.33 V (study N)
current_estimate: CALC (study N): the balanced candidate 2.48 V; the pass's 1.5 mm nib 3.33 V

title: Magnet temperature margin
requirement: The magnets stay >= 20 K below their grade's limit with the worst-case screen sustained at 35 deg in a 30 degC room
rationale: Study N's constraint (magnets below their grade's temperature), with a 20 K margin (docs/nib_optimisation.md s9.2)
current_estimate: CALC (study N): the balanced candidate 37.2 degC against N52's 80 degC

title: Ball writing drag
requirement: The ball's in-plane drag at N = F_n, mean over writing directions at 35 deg on the six papers, <= 30 mN; if higher, the nib budgets are re-run before the design freezes
rationale: The ball's drag makes about two thirds of the nib's heat in typical writing (72 % of the balanced candidate's typical load), and 1.5 x the ink force roughly doubles the loss (study N, CALC); study K's text said the weight dominated, but its sums set the weight aside in contact
current_estimate: CALC (study N): 28 mN in the model at F_n 0.196 N (PROPOSED DESIGN, gate G1; LIT CON-13 shapes)

title: Measured force constant
requirement: The measured weakest force per sqrt(W) over the usable disk is >= 0.7 x the image-method value (the derating in every claim)
rationale: The image-method model is an upper bound (ideal iron, images, no saturation, fringing or winding build); every nib figure derates it to 0.7 at its weakest point (DEC-080); every loss scales with 1 / derating^2 (study N)
current_estimate: CALC (study N, upper bound): the balanced candidate 0.272 N/sqrt(W) at the weakest point (0.398 / 0.409 at the centre), so >= 0.19 N/sqrt(W) measured

title: H1 regression check
requirement: After any change, sim2 reproduces H1 on H1's test grid: unmodified ink error within +/-10 %, oracle ratio within +/-0.03 in >= 90 % of cases
rationale: H1 stays the fast regression reference (DEC-040); tolerances written before the grid ran
current_estimate: 56 Rev H cases: unmodified error within 3.1 %; oracle ratio within +/-0.03 in 52 of 56 (93 %), worst +0.040 at 12 Hz; causal ratio within +/-0.05 in 50 of 56 (SIM)

title: Numerical convergence
requirement: At the production step, the ink path differs by <= 1 um rms from the half step; energy residual <= 1e-3 of the energy scale
rationale: Calculation verification (ASME V&V 40 sense); 100 us steps break down
current_estimate: 0.22 um rms at 25 us against 12.5 us (observed order 1.07); energy residual <= 6.8e-4 (SIM)

title: Labelled parameters and provenance
requirement: Every parameter carries a label and source (params.LABELS); every result file carries stabpen.provenance metadata
rationale: Every number must say where it comes from (Rev J plan s5)
current_estimate: Implemented in sim2/params.py; stage outputs carry provenance (docs/sim_v2.md s12)

title: Pen-only observations, sourced randomisation
requirement: The Gym observation holds only the pen's own sensor readings with their noise, bias and delay; every DR range cites its source
rationale: Policies trained in sim2 must see only what the pen can sense; an unsourced range hides an assumption
current_estimate: sim2/env.py: 25 randomised factors (results/sim2/env_benchmark.json)

title: Ranking only until validated
requirement: sim2 results are used only for COU-1 (ranking concepts and controllers) until EXP-V01, V02, V04 calibrate it and EXP-V05 passes
rationale: FDA 2023 framework and ASME V&V 40: evidence of benefit or safety (COU-3) is not supported now, and policy training for bench and human tests (COU-2) needs bench validation
current_estimate: No bench or human data: COU-1 only

title: Named comparators in every benefit study
requirement: Every study that supports a claim of benefit for any product option compares, per task and per user group, against an ordinary light pen, a weighted pen, typing on a phone or tablet with accessibility settings configured, and dictation where the task allows. Device studies add the device unpowered and the device locked with matched mass.
rationale: Passive utensils matched or beat active ones on preference (ACT-18, ACT-19); dictation is about 3 times faster than a phone keyboard for typical speakers (HAP-161) but made 36.3 % word errors on PD speech in a research test (PDT-104); engineering report section 7
current_estimate: No comparison run yet

title: Customer discovery before tooling
requirement: No tooling or volume-component commitment for the active pen until go/no-go criteria GNG-1 to GNG-5 (results/market/go_no_go_criteria.csv) have been evaluated in EXP-U01, EXP-U02 and EXP-U05 and reported to the lead.
rationale: Rev K needs 28 000-70 000 USD of tooling (docs/revK_design.md s5.4, ASSUMPTION); no demand evidence exists for pen users with tremor
verification: Lead review of the EXP-U01/U02/U05 reports
current_estimate: Not started

title: Price justified by willingness to pay
requirement: The active pen's target retail price does not exceed the highest tested price at which at least 20 % of the serviceable subgroup say they would definitely buy (GNG-5), unless a third-party payer route is secured in writing.
rationale: Rev K's cost implies about 508-1142 USD at a 50 % gross margin and 907-2039 USD retail with a 60 % margin and a 30 % channel margin (CALCULATION from docs/revK_design.md s5.4); passive writing aids cost 8-125 USD (PDT-107)
current_estimate: Implied price 508-2039 USD (CALCULATION)

title: Ready to write in seconds; usable when flat
requirement: Median time from picking up the pen to the first useful word is at most 10 s with no phone or app step for ordinary writing; with the battery flat (unpowered) the pen still writes with legibility non-inferior to an ordinary pen (lower 95 % bound of the difference at least -5 percentage points).
rationale: Everyday writing is short and frequent: median 18 words per occasion (HAP-159); 62 % of GB adults aged 65+ write lists by hand at least weekly (HAP-158). Rev K's unpowered nib rests on its stop 1.26 mm off centre (docs/claims_register.md). The 10 s threshold is an ASSUMPTION
current_estimate: Not measured

title: Design for paper-bound jobs, not text speed
requirement: Product requirements and messages prioritise the paper-bound jobs that EXP-U01 and EXP-U02 find unserved (expected: signatures, paper forms, cards, lists). Speed of long text entry against dictation or typing is not a design goal.
rationale: Signatures and paper documents remain required for wills, powers of attorney and postal votes in the UK (PDT-105) and are checked on US mail ballots (PDT-106); dictation is far faster for clear speakers (HAP-161)
current_estimate: Jobs not yet measured in the target group

title: Measuring pen: reliable, quick and separate from the consumer pen
requirement: A measuring pen for clinics or trials achieves test-retest ICC at least 0.80 for its primary writing metrics over 1-2 weeks in ET and in PD, correlation |rho| at least 0.5 with blinded clinical writing items, and a complete assessment in at most 10 minutes. It is a separate product with its own intended purpose and regulatory route; the consumer pen keeps REQ-USR-003 (no diagnostic output).
rationale: A tremor-measuring device is US Class II (21 CFR 882.1950) and monitoring or decision software is EU class IIa (MDCG 2021-24 Rule 11) (PDT-114); NICE prices PD monitors at GBP 64-225 per patient-month or use (PDT-115); tablet spiral measurement reached ICC 0.97 (PDT-12)
current_estimate: Not measured
trace: docs/market_and_users.md s6; results/market/competitors.csv C-19 to C-21

title: Outcomes payers can read
requirement: Every EXP-U device study records the Bain-Findley ADL writing item (or the TETRAS ADL writing item) and the MDS-UPDRS 2.7 patient item before and after, and QUEST 2.0 satisfaction, as secondary outcomes. Licences for each scale are confirmed before use.
rationale: A US Medicare coverage policy uses a Bain-Findley writing score of 3 or more for entry and a 1-point improvement for continuation (PDT-113)
current_estimate: Not collected

title: Intended purpose and classification for each option
requirement: Before any external claim, each product option has a written intended purpose, a classification rationale for the US (21 CFR 890.5050 with 890.9, or 882.1950) and for the EU and UK (MDR Annex VIII Rules 1, 11 and 13; UK MDR 2002), and marketing text that meets CAP Code section 12.
rationale: Classification depends on intended purpose and technology; an actuated pen may need a 510(k) under 890.9(b) (PDT-114); CAP 12.1 allows medical claims only for conformity-marked devices (PDT-119)
current_estimate: Not written

title: Honest discovery
requirement: No money or deposits are taken from patients or families before a benefit is shown; every participant-facing text states that the product is in development and unproven; all discovery results are reported, including no-go results.
rationale: MRS Code 2023 rules 4 and 23-26; CAP Code 12 (PDT-119); DEC-094
verification: Ethics review of all participant-facing texts; EXP-U05 audit
current_estimate: Not started

title: Children's products and studies
requirement: Products or studies for children compare against typing and standard occupational-therapy practice, measure unassisted handwriting legibility and speed at retention, never claim to treat dyslexia, and follow child-research safeguards (verified responsible-adult permission; the child's right to decline).
rationale: Effective handwriting programmes need practice (HAP-41); spelling, not movement, limits dyslexic writing (HAP-47, HAP-48); MRS Code rules 16-22 (PDT-119)
verification: EXP-U09 and any children's protocol review
current_estimate: Not started

title: Fine-stage travel
requirement: The fine stage gives at least +/-5 mm radial usable travel on the paper (soft limit, end stops beyond), enough that perfect knowledge of severe real tremor leaves at most 0.15 mm at the tip on the tuning split
rationale: DEC-086: tremor is cancelled on the fine stage only. With perfect knowledge at the severe class its 99th-percentile travel is 3.45 mm, and it spends 0.1 % of the contact time at the +/-5 mm soft limit (SIM, study P)
verification: EXP-PL01 (AC-PL01-01); simulation rerun on the built stage's identified model

title: Fine-stage dynamics
requirement: The fine stage follows position commands with >= 25 Hz bandwidth (40 Hz proposed), <= 0.6 kg moving per axis, >= 20 N peak and >= 5 N continuous per axis, first structural mode >= 150 Hz
rationale: DEC-086: one belt stage run at 15 Hz leaves 0.07 mm with perfect knowledge and 0.25 mm with the camera, against 0.02 and 0.09 mm for the voice-coil stage; belt axes ring at about 50 Hz (LIT CON-112) (SIM, study P)
current_estimate: Bandwidth 15 / 25 / 80 Hz with the camera: 0.24 (0.21 to 0.27) / 0.13 (0.12 to 0.15) / 0.07 (0.06 to 0.07) mm (40 Hz: 0.09 (0.08 to 0.10)); force RMS with perfect knowledge 2.08 (1.84 to 2.36) N (SIM)

title: Coarse stage
requirement: The coarse stage moves the fine stage +/-40 x +/-20 mm at <= 50 mm/s and <= 2 m/s^2 with feedforward of the accepted word's page motion; force capped at 20 N
rationale: DEC-086: the belt coarse stage carries the fine stage and moves the page through an accepted word (SIM, study P)
current_estimate: An accepted word up to 80 mm long passes under a still pen; the references span 'se' up to 11 x 7 mm and 5.7 s; 'library' up to 35 x 8 mm and 23.2 s (SIM references)

title: Absolute tip sensing
requirement: The tip sensor reports the pen tip in the desk frame with <= 6 ms latency, <= 15 um RMS noise per axis, >= 250 samples/s, a marker <= 3 mm from the ball (tilt error <= 5 % of the hand tremor) or tilt compensation
rationale: DEC-087: the camera's latency and noise set the camera loop's residual (SIM, study P); camera data MFR AMF-281, AMF-282; EMR under the plate is the alternative (AMF-98)
current_estimate: Latency 10 / 15 ms leaves 0.14 (0.12 to 0.15) / 0.20 (0.18 to 0.23) mm; noise 30 um 0.13 (0.11 to 0.14) mm; tilt 10 % 0.16 (0.14 to 0.18) mm (SIM, perfect separation)

title: Hold-down and registration
requirement: The sheet is held against >= 3 N of shear (A5: about 240 Pa of vacuum, CALC) with no slip under the ball's drag, and registered to the platen frame within 0.2 mm
rationale: The ball's friction ties the page to the pen: a hand resting on the moving paper runs the loop at its 20 N cap, and with only a clip the hand carries the sheet away (SIM, study P); LuGre creep inflates simulated slip (CON-113)
current_estimate: Palm rest and vacuum: the camera loop leaves 0.09 (0.08 to 0.10) mm, sheet slip 0.08 (0.07 to 0.10) mm; palm rest and a clip only: the sheet walks 1.4 (1.0 to 1.9) mm (page held) and 8.5 (7.3 to 10.1) mm (camera loop); hand on vacuum-held paper: the camera loop leaves 0.58 (0.43 to 0.72) mm at 20.0 (20.0 to 20.0) N RMS; hand on clip-held paper: the sheet travels 63 (46 to 79) mm (SIM; LuGre creep inflates slip, CON-113)

title: Palm rest
requirement: A fixed palm-rest bridge keeps the hand off the moving paper; underside 15-35 mm above the paper (25 mm nominal, the ISO 13854 finger gap), posts outside the plate's swept envelope
rationale: Keeps the hand off the moving paper (REQ-PLT-005); ISO 13854's finger gap (CON-110) (study P)
current_estimate: Design rule (CAD; ISO 13854 via CON-110); slip rows above

title: Pen holding in accepted mode
requirement: In accepted mode the pen is docked in a cradle, or held with the hand on the palm rest so that its tip moves <= 0.15 mm under the page's sliding drag (compliance x friction x normal force), with the normal force regulated at <= 0.5 N by the Z axis and the drag-decoupled ink-loop controller
rationale: DEC-088: a moving page drags a compliantly held pen through the ball; HW1's relaxed hand completes 0 of 20 accepted words, a docked pen 20 of 20 (SIM, study P)
current_estimate: 'se' proposed 20/20, cradle 20/20, relaxed hand 0/20 (SIM)

title: Contact and lift
requirement: Load cells under the plate detect contact (>= 50 mN) within 2 ms; the Z-drop breaks contact within 40 ms and the page makes no air move until the break is confirmed
rationale: Accepted writing needs every contact change confirmed before the page moves; the five-bar's lift is 200 ms (SIM, study P)
current_estimate: Air-phase ink at most 0.000 mm over all 1,735 simulated words (a 40 ms drop, 200 ms in one variant, against the plan's 200 ms lift phases) (SIM); the five-bar's lift is 200 ms

title: Safety
requirement: Force caps 20 N (fine and coarse, in hardware current limits), a 50 mm/s speed cap on the coarse stage (the fine stage follows tremor and is bounded by a 0.2 m/s slew limit, its +/-5 mm travel, its force cap and the kinetic-energy limit), moving kinetic energy <= 0.05 J, no fixed gap between 4 and 25 mm at a moving edge without a skirt, SELV supply, an emergency stop that holds the stage and drops the page; the page can only drag the pen with friction (<= 0.4 N)
rationale: ISO/TS 15066's 140 N for hands (CON-111) and ISO 13854's gaps (CON-110); a desk appliance near the user's hand (study P)
current_estimate: 20 N is 14 % of ISO/TS 15066's 140 N for hands (CON-111); 1.8 mJ at 50 mm/s (CALC)

title: Noise, power, size
requirement: <= 40 dB(A) at 0.5 m while writing; <= 25 W from a 24 V adapter; A5 footprint <= 380 x 300 mm, paper surface <= 70 mm above the desk
rationale: A desk appliance for home and clinic (study P s2.6, s6; CALC on ASSUMPTION ranges)
current_estimate: Budgets (CALC on ASSUMPTION ranges)
